In scenario 15 the table preferred a cut allocation by 3.02 kg/h, the polishing with true solves reversed it (+0.134); G at these three scenarios is about zero (0.000, -0.000, -0.002). The cap is not shown to matter (the polished values of the cut allocations are all worse); a better value among the cut allocations cannot be excluded for scenario 15.

**h) Reading (evidence, not proof) and caveats.** (1) The five largest gains of Befund 73 are not an artefact of a weak S2 or of the table search: they hold in every one of five seeds against the best S2 of 25 pairs of seeds (minimum G 4.9-16.9 kg CO2e/h). (2) They also hold, at 4.1-11.4 kg/h (minimum over the seeds), with the inlet temperature limited to the laboratory maximum of 100 degC; at 22-24 the gain falls by 19-35 % and the solution changes (the other line runs hot). The gains at 18 and 19 (5.5, 9.3 kg/h) lie wholly inside the laboratory range and do not touch a bound of the temperature. (3) They remain model results: the product of the hot line is dried to 0.036-0.090 kg/kg against the tightened limit 0.144 (over-drying; whether that is acceptable for the product is not tested), the exchanger that moves 240-580 kW from a humid exhaust of 50-73 degC to S1 is not modelled (only the cascade), the network parameters (`T_kalt`, `dT_min`, `eta_H`) and the scale factor are placeholders or scaling, line B is synthetic, the margin of B is an assumption (D8). The result is conditional on the lower bound 1.26 m/s (placeholder, Befunde 52, 69; 0.80 m/s not computed) and on the 25-point grid. (4) **The coupling gain is nevertheless NOT demonstrated by the rule over the 25 scenarios**, also with the more robust search (median 0.56 kg/h): the gain is concentrated in 5 warm or humid scenarios (G above 5 kg/h) and 5 more between 1.1 and 2.6 kg/h; in 10 scenarios it is zero within 0.002 kg/h. The five large gains stay EXPLORATORY in their origin (not formulated beforehand) until a test formulated beforehand confirms them; no number from this entry may be cited as a confirmed finding of a coupling gain in general. (5) Open: the shortlist of the 100 degC run is that of 120 degC; the search is multimodal (22, 24, 19 at 100 degC with one seed missing the optimum), the minima over the seeds are lower bounds.

Run-times (measured): first run 2 h 07 min (estimate 2.5 h), 18/19 run 50 min (45 min), sensitivity 1 h 47 min (1.8 h), the other 18 scenarios 10 h 03 min (9 h). Branch `m3x`, not merged.

**Addendum to Befund 73 (2026-10-08): two lists of scenarios, defined; the negative G at scenario 17 was a search shortfall; all G values are lower bounds.** Two lists of scenarios were used in this entry and in the instruction for the protection run, and they are not the same. (1) **The scenarios with the LARGEST gains**, defined as G above 5 kg CO2e/h in the control: **18, 19, 22, 23, 24** (G = 5.59, 9.41, 7.03, 11.90, 17.42 kg CO2e/h; section d and i of this entry). (2) **The scenarios with a material gain through ANOTHER INTERCONNECTION** (another allocation than S2 with `G_alloc` above 0.2 kg CO2e/h, section d): **16, 17, 22, 23, 24**. The status paragraph at the top of this entry ("the scenarios 16, 17, 22, 23, 24") names the second list but speaks of the large gains; the first list is the one meant there. The protection run (Befund 76) was started on the second list by mistake; the mix-up originated in the instruction, not in the run. Scenarios 18 and 19 were protected afterwards (Befund 76). **Scenario 17:** the negative G of -0.166 kg CO2e/h of the main seed was a search shortfall of the table search (section e); the direct search with five seeds (Befund 76) finds the M3' value 1152.71 in every seed. **All G values of this entry are lower bounds of the coupling gain** (the search is multimodal and the main seed gives upper bounds of the M3' value); a missing gain in a scenario can be a search shortfall. The verdict of this entry by the rule fixed beforehand stands as measured; its re-measurement with the direct five-seed search on all 25 scenarios is reported in Befund 76.

**Addendum to Befund 76 (2026-10-08): cold-side temperature.** All runs of Befund 73 and 76 (tables, joint searches, S2, direct five-seed searches, the 100 degC sensitivity) used the cold-side temperature of the condensing cascade `T_kalt` = **29.1 degC** (the default of `SiteSpec.t_kalt_celsius`, passed unchanged into every site evaluation, `joint_search.py`; no run overrides it). 29.1 degC is the more realistic of the values examined in Befund 52 (sweep 15 / 20 / 25 / 29.1 / 35 degC): **the large gains were won against the more realistic cold-side temperature, not against the optimistic 15 degC.** The value is still a placeholder of the network (`dT_min`, `eta_H` likewise), and the mechanism rests on the condensation, so a lower `T_kalt` would be expected to enlarge it and a higher one to reduce it; neither direction was computed.

### 77. Confirmatory test M4-C of the coupling gain at warm and humid ambient air: CONFIRMED by both criteria (K_lab 6 of 6, K_box 6 of 6 scenarios with G of at least 1.0 kg CO2e/h; smallest G over the seeds 2.88 kg CO2e/h at the box 60-100 degC); the negative controls show G about zero; the gain follows the absolute humidity of the ambient air (not separated from the temperature)

**a) Status and test set.** The hypothesis, the scenarios, the criteria, the candidate list and the script were fixed and committed BEFORE any of the scenarios was computed (`docs/09` section "Confirmatory test M4-C", commit `d09f8ce`; project lead, 2026-10-08, who released the runs the same day). **H1:** at warm and humid ambient air the joint optimum of the two lines (M3') saves more than 1.0 kg CO2e/h of the site against "each line on its own, then the best interconnection" (S2) in at least 5 of the 6 scenarios of group W. **Test set (named): NEW ambient points, none among the 25 Befund 52 points;** group W (decision rule): T_amb 30.0 and 32.5 degC x phi 0.60, 0.72, 0.82; group N (negative control, no rule): (32.5; 0.30), (30.0; 0.35); group H (descriptive, no rule): (20.0; 0.82), (25.0; 0.82). Lines A (1.5 kg/h) and B (2.0 kg/h), scaled site (k = 271.797, a scaling computation), no exchanger limit, cold-side temperature 29.1 degC (Addendum to Befund 76), lower gas-velocity bound 1.26 m/s (0.80 m/s NOT computed), margin m for both lines (D8, an assumption for B), nozzle pressure 1.0 bar. **Method of Befund 76, unchanged:** S2 = optimum of each line alone for the DE seeds 0-4, best S2 = minimum over the 25 pairs of seeds of the best of the 441 interconnections with true solves; M3' = joint DE + Nelder-Mead of the four set points on true solves for every candidate interconnection and every seed 0-4, best over the candidates; `G_s = value(best S2) - value(M3'(seed s))`, `G = min_s G_s`. Candidates per scenario (fixed): the two interconnections that M3' chose in the best solutions of the scenarios 18, 19, 22, 23, 24 (at the boxes 60-120 and 60-100 degC), plus the interconnection of the best S2 of the scenario (three per scenario). **Criteria:** K_lab (MAIN, box 60-100 degC, the laboratory range 50-100 degC): G at least 1.0 kg/h in at least 5 of 6 scenarios of W; K_box (second, box 60-120 degC, group W only): the same rule; both are reported, the statement for the conference rests on K_lab (above 100 degC the model extrapolates). A miss of K_lab would have meant: not confirmed, no recomputation, no change of a threshold.

**d) Search robustness.** In both boxes some seeds find a second, worse optimum (K_lab: seed 2 at (30.0; 0.60) with 2.88 against 6.94-7.02, at (30.0; 0.72) seeds 2 and 4 with 4.17 and 4.22 against 9.29-9.30, at (30.0; 0.82) seed 2 with 6.65 against 10.04-10.06, at (32.5; 0.60) seed 2 with 3.76 against 4.97-5.04; K_box: seed 3 at (32.5; 0.60) with 3.76 against 6.33-6.37). The criterion uses the minimum over the seeds, i.e. the weakest seed, so the gains are lower bounds of the search. **The criterion is met with the weakest seed in every scenario.**

**e) Negative controls N (no decision rule; the expectation G about zero was stated, not tested).** (32.5; 0.30), 0.0091 kg/kg: G over the seeds -0.105 to -0.002 kg/h (median -0.010); (30.0; 0.35), 0.0093 kg/kg: -0.171 to -0.005 (median -0.022). G is about zero (the small negative values are search shortfalls of single seeds, not an advantage of S2). Warm but dry air gives no gain.

**f) Group H (descriptive, no rule): temperature or absolute humidity?** (20.0; 0.82), 0.0120 kg/kg: G = 0.944 to 0.994 kg/h. (25.0; 0.82), 0.0164 kg/kg: G = 5.773 to 5.816 kg/h. With the other points: at about 0.016 kg/kg the gain is 5.6 (27.5 degC, phi 0.70, scenario 18, direct run of Befund 76: 0.0162 kg/kg), 5.8 (25 degC, phi 0.82) and 7.0 kg/h (30 degC, phi 0.60), i.e. ambient temperatures from 25 to 30 degC give gains of the same size at the same absolute humidity; at 0.0120 kg/kg (20 degC) it is 0.9; at 0.0141 kg/kg (35 degC, phi 0.40, scenario 21 of Befund 73, table search) it is +0.006; at 0.0091-0.0093 kg/kg (group N) it is zero. **Reading (evidence, not proof): the gain follows the absolute humidity of the ambient air rather than the temperature; it starts between about 0.014 and 0.016 kg/kg.** It is not a function of the absolute humidity alone: at 0.0186 kg/kg (32.5 degC, phi 0.60) the gain is 5.0 kg/h at the box 60-100 degC, less than 7.0 at 0.0160 kg/kg (30 degC), so the temperature has a further influence. A run that varies the absolute humidity at constant temperature (or the reverse) was not made; the statement rests on two points of group H.

**g) The best solutions (descriptive; box 60-100 degC).** One line is run hot and dry, the other stays near its own optimum. The hot line is line B at (30.0; 0.60), (30.0; 0.72), (30.0; 0.82) and (32.5; 0.60) with 93.7 / 98.7 / 100.0 / 100.0 degC, and line A at (32.5; 0.72) and (32.5; 0.82) with 94.3 and 98.6 degC (line B then 81.5 and 78.0 degC). The product moisture of the hot line is 0.043-0.080 kg/kg against the tightened limit 0.144, i.e. 0.064 to 0.101 kg/kg below it (over-dried); that of the other line is 0.117-0.144 kg/kg (at the limit in three of six scenarios). The gas velocity is 1.3-1.4 m/s in the rounded printout of the evaluation, at or near the lower bound 1.26 m/s (not checked to the third digit); the nozzle pressure is fixed (D6). This is the mechanism of Befund 76 (the humid exhaust of the hot line gives condensing heat to the external sink, the external exhaust Q1 is released for the inlet air of the lines); the heat flows of these scenarios were not evaluated.

**h) Reading and caveats (evidence, not proof).** (1) **H1 is confirmed in the model for the test set named:** warm and humid air (absolute humidity 0.016-0.026 kg/kg; 30.0 and 32.5 degC), lines A and B, the scaled site, 1.26 m/s, `T_kalt` = 29.1 degC. In all six scenarios of W and in both boxes the gain over S2 holds with the weakest seed (2.88 to 11.33 kg/h at the box 60-100 degC, 3.76 to 15.77 kg/h at 60-120 degC), and the negative controls show no gain. The large gains of Befund 73 and 76 are therefore not an artefact of the selection that found them. (2) **It is a confirmation in the simulator, not in the plant.** The same model produced the gains and this test. The physical effect (condensing recovery from a humid exhaust; the exchanger is not modelled, only the cascade) and the over-dried product (0.04-0.08 kg/kg against the limit 0.144; whether that is acceptable for the product is open) are not tested against plant data; line B is synthetic, the network parameters (`T_kalt`, `dT_min`, `eta_H`) are placeholders, the lower gas-velocity bound is a placeholder, the scale factor is a scaling computation. (3) The test does not change the verdict of Befund 73 and its re-measurement in Befund 76 g): the coupling gain over all 25 grid scenarios is NOT demonstrated by the rule (median 0.56 kg/h). The gain exists in the warm and humid part of the weather range; in the dry part it is about zero. (4) Three candidate interconnections per scenario (not all 441 for M3'); N and H at the box 60-100 degC only. (5) Not computed: 0.80 m/s; other `T_kalt`; the exchanger duty limits (c = 0.5-1.5 of Befund 73) at these scenarios; the plant.
Artifacts (`artifacts/runs/`): `m4c_confirm_lab_umin126`, `m4c_confirm_box_umin126`. Commits: `d09f8ce` (the fixed test, before the runs), `29db2cc` and `0ef03f0` (raw records and verdicts). Run-time (measured): K_lab 10:13 to 14:53 on 2026-10-08, about 4 h 40 min (estimate 3.5-4.8 h); K_box 14:53 to 17:37, about 2 h 45 min (estimate 2-2.8 h). Branch `m4c`, not merged.

### 78. Review of 2026-10-09, findings A1 and K1 checked on the stored solutions: the cascade checks the minimum approach temperature only at the warm end of a stage, and the confirmed gain of Befund 77 does NOT hold at the reported solutions when the approach is checked along the whole exchanger; the solver bound `T_bed >= T_amb + 10 K` cuts off valid drying states at warm ambient air. The conclusion of Befund 77 is SUSPENDED until a re-optimisation

**a) Status and scope.** Three independent reviews of master `c7c9621` (2026-10-09) are filed verbatim under `docs/reviews/2026-10-09/`, their findings registered in `docs/12_review_2026-10-09.md`. Two of them can overturn core results (stage 1, decision of the project lead): **A1** (review 3) -- `heatnetwork/balance.py` (about l. 545-547) limits a stage only by `T_sink,out <= T_source,in - dT_min` (warm end), never at the cold end or along the exchanger; **K1** (review 2, also the cross-cutting finding of review 1) -- the outer bisection of `simulation/steady_state.py` (about l. 300-302) searches the bed temperature only from `T_amb + 10 K`. Decision of the project lead (2026-10-09): **check only, on stored solutions; no correction in `src/`, no re-optimisation.** Both findings are **confirmed** by the checks below (`docs/12`: status "confirmed"). Rules: scripts committed before they ran, clean tree, artifacts under new names, `git/dirty=False`; the stored figures were reproduced before anything was changed in the computation (differences 0.0).

**b) A1, method (script `scripts/check_review_a1_cascade_approach.py`, commit `db79a02`; artifact `review_a1_cascade_approach_m4c_lab`).** Input: every S2 record (25 pairs of seeds) and every joint record (3 candidate interconnections x 5 seeds) of Befund 77 at the box 60-100 degC (`m4c_confirm_lab_umin126`, groups W, N, H). The line states are re-solved at the stored set points; every stored CO2 value is reproduced exactly. Two profiles of a source, both releasing the same total heat down to `T_kalt`: the **model profile** that the cascade assumes (sensible cooling to `T_kalt`, then all latent heat at `T_kalt`) and the **physical profile** (condensation from the dew point of the exhaust on; discretised in steps of 0.01 K). Counter-current stage; the approach at a point is the source temperature minus the sink temperature there. A corrected cascade, in the script only, enforces `dT_min` as the minimum along the whole exchanger on the physical profile (`along`); with the check at the warm end and the model profile the same code reproduces `evaluate_cascade` for all 441 interconnections at every reported solution (largest difference 4.5e-13 kg/h).

**c) A1, results.** (1) **Stages of the reported W solutions (best S2, best M3' of every seed), cascade as run, `dT_min` 20 K:** every stage line exhaust -> S1 that carries heat violates 20 K along the exchanger, in both arms; the stages of the external source Q1 hold exactly 20 K (warm end binding).

| arm | stage | stages below 20 K | approach at the cold end (model profile) | minimum along the exchanger (physical profile) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M3' | LA -> S1 | 30 of 30 | 4.79-14.10 K | 0.14-15.63 K |
| M3' | LB -> S1 | 30 of 30 | 6.59-14.10 K | 4.29-15.73 K |
| S2 | LA -> S1 | 6 of 6 | 14.10 K | 12.88-15.24 K |
| S2 | LB -> S1 | 6 of 6 | 14.22-19.84 K | 14.46-19.84 K |

(2) **G at held set points** (kg CO2e/h; G = min over the five seeds of best S2 - M3'(seed), the rule of Befund 77; the best of the 441 interconnections at the held set points in both arms):

| W scenario (T_amb / phi) | G as reported | G, `dT_min` 20 K along the exchanger | G, `dT_min` 10 K along the exchanger |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30.0 / 0.60 | 2.88 | -0.93 | -0.00 |
| 30.0 / 0.72 | 4.17 | -19.83 | -12.46 |

With the stored interconnections held (instead of the best of the 441): 0 of 6 at 20 K, 1 of 6 at 10 K. The negative controls N stay about zero (-0.11, -0.17 at 20 K); group H: -2.29 and -9.48 at 20 K. The best S2 itself changes in three W scenarios (30.0 / 0.72: 1155.97 -> 1158.88; 30.0 / 0.82: 1156.61 -> 1162.00; 32.5 / 0.82: 1157.10 -> 1158.15 kg CO2e/h at 20 K). (3) **Scenario (30.0; 0.82), the hot line:** as run, the hot line (B in seeds 0, 1, 3, 4: inlet 100 degC, exhaust 57.6 degC, dew point 35.9 degC; A in seed 2: 94 degC, 60.7 degC, 34.1 degC) gives 357 kW to S1 and condenses about 254 kg/h (scaled; seed 2: 343 kW, 198 kg/h), at a smallest approach of 5.5 K (seed 2: 2.1 K); S1 enters that stage at 20.0 degC (seed 2: 23.8 degC) because the other line's stage comes first. **With 20 K along the exchanger the hot line does not condense at all** (0 kg/h in every seed, with the stored and with the best interconnection): S1 enters at 16.9-18.3 degC, so the exhaust may not fall below 36.9-38.3 degC, above its dew point. With 10 K: 25.5-25.8 kg/h in the stored interconnection, 0 kg/h in the best one (the hot line then feeds SB). In S2 at 10 K the best interconnection condenses 252 kg/h of line B into S1, which then enters at 15 degC.

**d) A1, reading.** **The confirmed gain of Befund 77 does not hold at the reported solutions when the minimum approach temperature is checked along the whole exchanger** (0 of 6 W scenarios at 20 K and at 10 K). It rests on condensation of line exhaust into S1 at approach temperatures of a few kelvin, which the warm-end check admits. **The conclusion of Befund 77 ("H1 confirmed in the model") is suspended until a re-optimisation under the corrected cascade.** Caveat: at held set points the figures are NOT a new coupling gain. The S2 figures are exact under the corrected cascade (the S2 set points are the optima of each line on its own, independent of the network, and the best interconnection was chosen anew); M3' would have to be re-optimised. Since the S2 set points are a candidate of the joint search, a corrected joint optimum gives a gain of at least max(0, G at held set points); whether some other joint optimum gains under the corrected cascade is open. Every result computed with the cascade is affected in principle (Befunde 57 d, 60, 69 b, 70, 71, 73, 76, 77); their figures are re-evaluated in a separate inventory.

**e) K1, method (script `scripts/check_review_k1_solver_bracket.py`, commit `fc03124`, probes below the inlet box minimum recorded as not evaluable in `caeea88` after the first run had aborted there without writing an artifact; artifact `review_k1_solver_bracket`).** (1) Every reported line solution of the artifacts of Befunde 69, 73, 76, 77 (17 artifacts, 1327 line solutions, 1037 distinct) re-solved at its stored set points with the search precision (30 / 1e-7); stored bed temperatures and product moistures reproduce exactly. A solution is ON THE BOUND iff `|T_bed - T_amb - 10| <= 1e-3 K`. (2) Every distinct solution on the bound (all, not a sample) probed with wider brackets of the outer bisection (lower edge `T_amb` + 5, + 3, + 0, - 5 K) at the stored set points and with the inlet temperature of that line lowered by 1, 2 and 5 K (other set points held; below 60 degC not evaluable, the config admits only [60, 120] degC). Regime: DRYING iff `Y_in < Y_out < Y_s(T_bed)`.

**f) K1, results.** (1) **301 of 1327 reported line solutions (212 distinct) lie on `T_amb + 10 K`** (18 within 1e-6 K); a further 40 lie within 0.1 K and are not counted. All are drying states. By artifact (on the bound / solutions): Befund 69: `m1_margin_cost_l015` 8 / 75, `m1_margin_cost_l020` 18 / 75, `m1_margin_cost_l015_umin126` 17 / 75, `m1_anchor_s05` 0 / 3; Befund 73: `m3_line_b_optimum_umin126` 5 / 25, `m3_joint_control_umin126` 22 / 100, `c0.5` 24 / 100, `c1.0` 23 / 100, `c1.5` 24 / 100, `m3_joint_seeds_umin126` 15 / 96, `m3_check_umin126` 2 / 26; Befund 76: `m3x_confirm_evaluation_umin126` 29 / 60, `m3x_confirm_s18_19_evaluation_umin126` 0 / 24, `m3x_sens_tmax100_evaluation_umin126` 19 / 60, `m3x_robust_rest_evaluation_umin126` 31 / 216; Befund 77: `m4c_confirm_lab_umin126` 38 / 120, `m4c_confirm_box_umin126` 26 / 72. At 1.26 m/s (Befund 69) M0 and M lie on the bound at 8 of 25 points each (27.5 degC at phi 0.25, 0.40, 0.55; all five points at 35 degC), the fixed point F at (35.0; 0.25); in Befund 77 line A of the S2 reference in 5 of 6 W scenarios (not at (30.0; 0.82)), in M3' mostly the line that is not run hot, in the negative controls both lines. (2) **At the stored set points** the wider brackets find the same solution. **With the inlet temperature lowered by 1 / 2 / 5 K** the default solver fails in every evaluable probe (211 of 211, 211 of 211, 209 of 209; not evaluable below 60 degC: 1, 1, 3), while the wider brackets with lower edges `T_amb` + 5, + 3, + 0 find a converged steady state (largest residual 1.6e-9) in every probe, the same root for every edge (largest difference 1.5e-5 K), **in the drying regime in every probe**, with the bed 0.3-4 K below the bound (`T_bed - T_amb` 9.17-9.71 / 8.34-9.42 / 5.96-8.53 K); the product moisture rises (below the tightened limit 0.144 in 159 / 132 / 61 of the probes), the CO2 of the line alone (gas heater, lab scale, no network) falls by 0.0035-0.0085 kg/h at -1 K and 0.017-0.039 kg/h at -5 K. The lower edge `T_amb - 5 K` fails in 64 of 212 cases (the inner moisture bisection finds no sign change there).

**g) K1, reading.** The bound `T_amb + 10 K` cuts off valid drying states; the optimisers saw them as solver failures, so the reported optima on the bound are set by a solver convention, not by the physics or a constraint. The reason given in the code comment and in `oracle_search.evaluate_point` (the condensation branch near ambient) holds below the ambient temperature, not in the band `T_amb` ... `T_amb + 10 K` (for `T_bed > T_amb` the inlet air is below saturation at the bed temperature). In which direction G (Befunde 73, 76, 77), the regret and the remaining control benefit (Befund 69) would move is NOT computed: in both arms solutions are cut off (in Befund 69 at 1.26 m/s M0 at 8 points and the fixed point F, whose inlet temperature 74.25 degC is set at (35.0; 0.25)).

**h) Not done, next.** No correction in `src/`, no re-optimisation. The inventory of every Befund that uses the cascade (figures re-evaluated with the check along the exchanger at 20 and 10 K) and a design of the corrections of A1 and K1 (not implemented) follow and are reported to the project lead first. Caveats: held set points throughout; the physical profile uses the heat-capacity rate and the latent heat at `T_kalt` of the cascade (the same totals as the model profile); the exchanger itself is not modelled (only the cascade with an approach temperature); `dT_min`, `T_kalt`, `eta_H`, the scale factor and line B remain placeholders or synthetic.

### 79. Corrections of the review findings K1 and A1 in `src/` (released by the project lead, 2026-10-09): the steady-state solver searches below `T_amb + 10 K` only where it used to fail (every old solution bit-identical), the cascade checks `dT_min` along the whole exchanger (the old cascade kept as a legacy mode that reproduces old artifacts bit for bit); provenance names both; the corrected cascade costs about 13 times more per call, the polishing objective is unchanged

**a) Status and rules.** Design `docs/13_design_corrections_a1_k1.md`, released by the project lead on 2026-10-09 with: fallback interval `[T_amb + 0.5, T_amb + 10]` only at a negative residual at `T_amb + 10`, regime check after the solution, bit-identity wherever the old solver found a solution; `approach_check = "along_exchanger"` as the default, `"warm_end"` only to reproduce old artifacts, 400 profile nodes plus an exact dew-point node, the discretisation error of the stage duty stated as a number; provenance in every new artifact; old and new figures never mixed in one table. Every step its own commit, the full suite before every push. Work in a local worktree (`fix-a1k1`), fast-forwarded into master.

**b) K1 (commit `9dec7cb`).** `solve_steady_state` keeps the first bracket `[T_amb + 10, max(T_in, T_susp) + 5]`; only if the energy residual is negative at both edges (the root lies below `T_amb + 10`, the case in which the solver failed with "kein Vorzeichenwechsel") it searches `[T_amb + 0.5, T_amb + 10]`. The two edge evaluations are handed to the bisection, so the computation is otherwise unchanged. After the solution, two new infeasibility reasons: no drying regime (`Y_in < Y_out < Y_s(T_bed)` violated) and a bed temperature on the lower search bound; new fields `lower_search_bound_celsius`, `bed_temperature_fallback_used`, `drying_regime`. Physical reason of the new lower bound: the inlet air carries the ambient absolute humidity, `Y_in <= Y_s(T_amb) < Y_s(T_bed)` for every `T_bed > T_amb`. **Verification (artifact `verify_corrections_a1_k1`, a): 1037 distinct stored line solutions of the artifacts of Befunde 69, 73, 76, 77, re-solved: bed temperature and product moisture identical (`==`) in 1037 of 1037, the fallback used in 0, all 1037 feasible, including the 212 on the old bound.** The K1 probe point of Befund 78 (line A, 35 degC / 0.25, inlet 73.25 degC) now solves at `T_bed - T_amb` = 9.20 K, drying, feasible. **Changed tests:** (i) the trap test at grid point 15 of Befund 52: the solver DEFAULTS (100 / 1e-13) now solve there through the fallback (a few 1e-6 K below `T_amb + 10`; `energy_target` within 1e-6 relative of Befund 52, not bit-identical); the search precision is unchanged; (ii) four failure-path tests of the bandit environment used 60 degC / 0.8 m/s at 20 degC / 0.5 as the "known failing point"; the corrected solver finds a wet, infeasible steady state there (product moisture 0.79 kg/kg), so the failure path is now tested at 35 degC / 0.5, where no drying state exists above `T_amb + 0.5`. Consequence for the RL environments (Befunde 62, 68): points that returned the failure sentinel can now return a penalised infeasible value; their reported results were computed with the old solver and are not re-run.

**c) A1 (commit `84d2b82`).** New module `heatnetwork/approach.py`. Source profile: `q(T) = C (T_out - T) + m max(0, Y - Y_s(T)) dh_v(T_kalt)` (condensing; linear to the dew-point floor in the sensible mode), nodes `T_out`, the dew point as an exact node and 400 nodes down to the floor; the totals equal those of MA1 (the available heat per source is unchanged). Stage duty: the largest duty with an approach of at least `dT_min` at every point of the counter-current exchanger, in closed form from the running minimum of `g(q) = T_src(q) + q / C_sink`, vectorised over the time steps. New result arrays `stage_min_approach_k`, `stage_pinch_position`; `SiteSpec.approach_check`, `approach_profile_nodes` and `SiteSpec.fingerprint`; `site_network.evaluate_site` builds the profiles once for all interconnections; `joint_search.site_spec_with_cap` keeps every field (it rebuilt `SiteSpec` field by field and would have dropped the new one). **Tests:** cold end binding (exact duty `C_source (T_out - T_in - dT_min)`), pinch inside the exchanger at the dew point (exact duty, position strictly inside), the minimum approach on a fine grid (40000-node profile, 20001 points per stage, two sources and two sinks in random order), one stage never recovers more than the warm-end check, available heat equal in both modes, the legacy mode reproduces stored M4-C values with `==`. Tests that pin the warm-end or flash semantics run in the legacy mode (MA1 formula, flash condensation, the M2 reproduction); the section count of the config fingerprint is 13. **Discretisation error of the stage duty at 400 nodes against 40000 (artifact `verify_corrections_a1_k1`, c): at most 2.9e-6 relative, 0.00046 kW absolute, over 375 random condensing stages with a duty.** **Legacy reproduction (b): 400 of 400 S2 and joint records of `m4c_confirm_lab_umin126` give the stored CO2 with `==`.** **Correction of the figures of Befund 78:** the check script of Befund 78 used a 0.01 K grid without an exact dew-point node; where the pinch sits at the dew point it cuts the kink, an error of the script, not of the corrected cascade (d): largest CO2 difference 0.0167 / 0.00083 / 0.000051 kg/h at the grid steps 0.01 / 0.001 / 0.0001 K. The figures of Befund 78 and of its inventory carry this error (at most about 0.02 kg/h), which does not touch any reading there.

**d) Provenance (commit `82e5880`).** `scripts/verify/_common.provenance(heat_network)` records `solver/bed_temperature_bracket`, `heatnetwork/approach_check` and `heatnetwork/fingerprint` (the `SiteSpec` of the run; "not used" for runs without a network; `None` = not recorded, the scripts written before Befund 79). Old and new figures are never mixed in one table.

**e) Run-time of the corrected cascade (script `scripts/probe_cascade_runtime.py`; artifact `probe_cascade_runtime_2`, `git/dirty=False`; single-threaded, CPU load 2-4 %; median over four solution states of M4-C, median of 5 rounds).** A first measurement (artifact `probe_cascade_runtime`) is invalid for the table objective: its set points fell into table cells without value, so the call returned the failure value without a cascade; it is kept as a record.

| per call | warm end | along the exchanger | ratio (median) |
|---|---|---|---|
| one cascade (one interconnection, profiles built in the call) | 0.21 ms | 3.0 ms | 14.6 |
| site evaluation of all 441 interconnections | 72 ms | 551 ms | 7.6 |
| objective of the table search (`table_objective`) | 0.23 ms | 3.3 ms | 12.7 |
| objective of the polishing (`evaluate_true`, two steady-state solves) | 0.41 s | 0.35 s | 0.88 |

The polishing is dominated by the steady-state solves (0.18 s each) and does not change; the table search becomes about 13 times more expensive. Estimate for a full nested search: see the draft of the coupling test (`docs/14_draft_m4r_coupling_test.md`).

**f) Order variants of the interconnections (found while drafting the new coupling test; reported, not corrected).** `joint_search.nested_search` treats the two orders of the stages `Q1 -> SA` and `Q1 -> SB` as the same problem when there is no exchanger limit ("the order cannot matter") and searches only one of them. At the reported solutions of M4-C the two orders give different site CO2 (by more than 1e-6 kg/h) in 1344 of 5880 pairs with the warm-end check and in 1512 of 5880 with the check along the exchanger (largest difference 14.9 kg/h in both) (artifact `verify_corrections_a1_k1`, e): Q1 is cooled by `Q1 -> S1` first, so its second stage to a line is limited by `dT_min`. The control of Befund 73 used this shortcut; S2 is not affected (every one of the 441 interconnections is evaluated), M3' may have missed the better order (its G would then be a lower bound, as already stated). Not recomputed; the draft of the new coupling test searches both orders.

**g) Anchor of M1 under the corrected solver** (artifact `m1_anchor_s05_k1`, see Befund 80): grid points 0 and 12 reproduce `s05_limit015_oracle_and_fixed` bit for bit, point 24 (35 degC / 0.85) does not (energy 0.970970 against 0.970946 kW, +2.4e-5 kW): the DE now evaluates candidates that failed before, so its path changes (the search is not converged by design, as in Befund 52); the solver gives the same values where it found solutions before (b).

**c) Reading by the rule of Befund 69, applied unchanged** (a statement is stable iff it points in the same direction at both bounds and its figure changes by less than half; `analyze_m1_gas_bound_sensitivity.py --suffix _k1`):

| S3 "most of the control benefit survives the margin" | stable | **stable** (changes 10-11 %) |
| overall | partly stable | **partly stable** |

**d) What changes and why.** At 1.26 m/s the old solver bound cut off the drying states below `T_amb + 10 K` at the warm points: 8 of the 25 optima M0 and M lay on it (Befund 78). With the fallback the oracle reaches lower inlet temperatures there (8 optima now below the old bound), dries less and hits the moisture limit more often (13 instead of 7 points); where the limit binds the margin costs about 1.5 %, so the median cost over all points is no longer 0. The fixed point, which was set by the solver bound at (35.0; 0.25), moves from 74.25 to 71.28 degC (5 of its 25 points now below the old bound) and costs less, so the regret at 1.26 m/s falls (median 19.8 -> 16.5 %). At 0.80 m/s the figures move little in the median (regret 8.3 -> 9.0 %, cost 1.30 % unchanged), but the upper tail grows (regret p95 11.9 -> 19.1 %, cost max 1.81 -> 3.04 %) and the moisture limit binds at all 25 points. **The structural finding of the second addendum to Befund 69 ("the lower bound of the gas velocity determines the optimum, independent of its value") weakens:** the optimum sits on the lower gas bound at 22 (M0) and 21 (M) of 25 points at 1.26 m/s (25 / 25 before) and at 17 / 20 at 0.80 m/s (21 / 22 before); at the other points it is now the moisture limit that sets it. **The conditional statements of Befund 69 change accordingly:** the cost of the margin per binding point (1.3-1.6 % before) is now also the median over all points at both bounds (1.30 / 1.46 %), i.e. the margin costs energy at both bounds; the regret at the laboratory minimum is about 16-17 % (median and pooled), not 18-20 %; the share of the control benefit that survives the margin is 94 % at 1.26 and 85 % at 0.80 m/s.

**e) Anchor (artifact `m1_anchor_s05_k1`).** The legacy objective at grid points 0 and 12 reproduces `s05_limit015_oracle_and_fixed` bit for bit; point 24 (35 degC / 0.85) does not: energy 0.970970 against 0.970946 kW (+2.4e-5 kW, +0.0025 %), inlet 92.99 against 93.02 degC. The solver gives identical values where it found solutions before (Befund 79, 1037 of 1037); the DE path changes because candidates that failed before are now evaluated, and the search is not converged by design (as Befund 52). The anchor was run as information, not as a gate (the gate of Befund 69 tested the new code path against the solver of that time).

**f) Caveats.** One line, steady state, no network (as M1); two bound values; the fixed point is searched anew; the 0.80 m/s bound is a placeholder below the laboratory range (Befund 52 addendum); the box minimum 60 degC binds at 12 / 8 points at 1.26 m/s and is itself a placeholder (`docs/02`); critical moisture 0.20 placeholder with its double role; the optimiser budget is exhausted by design, the DE seed spread is not measured here. The figures of Befund 69 stay as written (append-only); they hold for the solver with the bound `T_amb + 10 K`. **Use from now on: the figures of this entry; Befund 69 only as the record of the old solver.**
Run-times (measured, 16 workers): anchor 6 min, 1.26 m/s 51 min, 0.80 m/s 53 min (estimate about 2 h for both). The two arms ran under a driver started independently of the session (log `C:/twinlink_runs/status.log`, not in the repository), which committed every artifact before the next stage. Commits: `c5f2949` (scripts, before the runs), `fec9829` (anchor), `2a1d806` (1.26 m/s), `c7e6b6a` (0.80 m/s), `bc681f3` (rule), `603cf69` (comparison).

**Addendum to Befund 69 (2026-10-09): re-computed with the corrected solver in Befund 80.** The figures of this entry and its addenda were computed with the steady-state solver whose search began at `T_amb + 10 K` (Befunde 78, 79: K1); 8 of the 25 optima at 1.26 m/s and the fixed point lay on that bound. Befund 80 re-computes M1 at both bounds with every other setting unchanged: by the unchanged stability rule S2 ("the margin costs energy") becomes stable (cost 1.30 / 1.46 % in the median), S1 stays not stable (regret 9.0 / 16.5 % in the median), S3 stays stable (85 / 94 %); the moisture limit binds at 25 / 13 of 25 points; the statement "the lower bound determines the optimum, independent of its value" holds only at 22 / 17 of 25 points. The assumption does not hold: at the stored solutions of M4-C the two orders give a different site CO2 in 1344 of 5880 pairs already with the cascade of this entry (warm-end check), by up to 14.9 kg CO2e/h (artifact `verify_corrections_a1_k1`, e), because Q1 is cooled by `Q1 -> S1` first and its second stage to a line is then limited by `dT_min`. **Consequence for this entry:** S2 is not affected (every one of the 441 interconnections was evaluated); M3' of the control may have missed the better order of the stages, so the values of M3' are upper bounds and **the G of the control are rather lower bounds** (in line with the addendum of 2026-10-08). The limited cases c = 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 searched both orders. Nothing is recomputed here; the re-fixed coupling test M4-R searches both orders as separate problems.

The stages that carry heat are those of S2 in 9 of 10 scenarios; the smallest approach over them is 10.0 K in every best M3'. **d) Plausibility (G cannot be clearly negative by construction: the S2 set points are a candidate of M3').** At 20 K no G is below -0.2 kg/h (smallest -0.020). **At 10 K two seed values are flagged as possible search shortfalls:** seed 4 at (30.0; 0.72), -0.410 kg/h, and seed 4 at (32.5; 0.60), -0.839 kg/h (the other seeds there reach 0.28-0.77 and -0.18 to 0.25 kg/h); these two seeds set the minimum of their scenarios. The criterion uses the weakest seed by design; the descriptive count of the 10 K case is unchanged by them (1 of 6 with either estimator).

**e) Checks.** (i) The exchanger limit of 1e12 kW: every reported solution (best S2 and M3' of every seed, 60 values per case) re-evaluated without a limit gives the identical value (`==`, asserted by the script). (ii) Tables (20 K; direct DE on true solves, four variables, seed 0, for the interconnection of the best M3'): (32.5; 0.82) direct 1157.564 against 1157.227 of the nested search, (30.0; 0.82) 1162.033 against 1162.002 kg CO2e/h: the single direct search does not reach the value of the nested search (+0.34, +0.03 kg/h); no sign of a table error (the direct DE with one seed certifies nothing beyond that). (iii) Windows of the polishing: never widened (5.0 kg/h in every search); 6-51 interconnections polished per search. (iv) Solver fallback used in the reported solutions: line A in most W scenarios and both lines in N; the K1 correction is active exactly where Befund 78 found the old bound.

**f) Reading.** **H1 is not confirmed in the corrected model** (K_R: 0 of 6). With the minimum approach temperature enforced along the whole exchanger at 20 K, the joint optimum of the two lines coincides with "each line on its own, then the best interconnection" in every scenario; the mechanism of Befunde 76 and 77 (one line run hot so that its humid exhaust condenses into S1 at approach temperatures of a few kelvin) is excluded by the check. **The large gains of Befunde 73, 76 and 77 do not survive the corrections A1 and K1**; by the rule fixed for M4-R this is final (no recomputation, no change of a threshold). The conclusion of Befund 77, suspended since Befund 78, is therefore withdrawn. At `dT_min` 10 K (an optimistic exchanger) a small coupling gain appears (W up to 1.2 kg/h, H up to 3.6 kg/h, at most 0.33 % of the site CO2), concentrated at mild humid air rather than at warm humid air; it is a sensitivity without a verdict. **Caveats:** a simulator result (scaled site, line B synthetic, `T_kalt`, `dT_min`, `eta_H`, the gas-velocity bound and the box minimum 60 degC are placeholders; the box minimum binds for line A at 10 K); three groups of ambient points only; the nested search is a search (lower bounds of G per seed; two flagged seed values at 10 K).

**g) Run-time.** Estimate before the run (`docs/09`): about 10 h (7-14 h). **Measured: 20 K 12 h 44 min, 10 K 11 h 00 min, 23 h 44 min in total** (14:56 on 2026-10-09 to 14:40 on 2026-10-10), i.e. about 2.4 times the estimate: the line optima for S2 (100 searches, about 8.5 min each) and the polishing of 6-51 interconnections per search took longer than the estimate assumed from Befund 73.
Artifacts: `m4r_test_dt20_umin126`, `m4r_test_dt10_umin126`. Commits: `c2d55dd` (fixed test), `65dcb7e`, `609a629` (artifacts), merged into master by `d0e535e`; full suite on the merge commit: **685 passed, 2 skipped in 914.71 s**.

**Addendum to Befund 77 (2026-10-12): the conclusion of this entry is withdrawn (Befund 81).** The conclusion "H1 is confirmed in the model", suspended since Befund 78, is withdrawn: the re-fixed coupling test M4-R in the corrected model (Befund 79: `dT_min` checked along the whole exchanger, solver with the fallback bracket), with the full nested search over all 441 interconnections and five seeds, misses its criterion K_R (G >= 1.0 kg CO2e/h in at least 5 of 6 W scenarios at `dT_min` 20 K) with 0 of 6; G lies between -0.02 and +0.002 kg CO2e/h and the joint optimum equals S2 (Befund 81). The gains of this entry rested on condensation of line exhaust into S1 at approach temperatures of a few kelvin. At `dT_min` 10 K (sensitivity, no verdict) 1 of 6 W scenarios reaches 1.0 kg/h. The verdict K_lab 6 of 6 stays the record of the run of this entry; no figure of this entry is to be cited as a coupling gain.

### 82. Preparation for the studies on sim-to-real transfer and experiment design: paired resolution, planned future inputs and an own solid-fraction process as options (review C1, C2, D1, E3), and a guard on where the code is loaded from

**a) Status and scope.** Instruction of the project lead (2026-10-12): three findings of the review of 2026-10-09 (`docs/12`) must be corrected before two new studies that compare methods over seeds and generate new data (A: pre-training on the grey-box simulator and post-training on a structurally different "plant"; B: which excitation gives the most information per run, including active learning). Corrected **as options**; no default was changed, **no older finding was re-computed**. Every older entry that rests on the old resolution formula (`evaluation/resolution.py`, unpaired, z, spread of the persistence only) or on the old data (future inputs clipped by the fluidisation bounds; solid fraction in phase with the ambient temperature) keeps its wording and its numbers; they were produced with the old formula and the old data.

**b) C1/C2 -- paired resolution (`cd7b562`).** New module `evaluation/paired_resolution.py` (`paired_comparison`, `paired_values`, `paired_verdicts`): all methods run with the same `master_seed`; paired differences `d_i = reference - candidate` per seed; t statistic with `n - 1` degrees of freedom; resolved if `|mean d|` exceeds `t * s_d / sqrt(n)` (`ddof=1`). Fewer than two pairs or differences without spread return "not resolved" instead of a threshold of 0 (review C4); the seed sets of the methods must be identical (no silent dropping); the metric has no default. The test is on the **mean** of the differences, the lab book reports medians; no correction for multiple comparisons (review item C-L1 stays open). `resolution.py` is unchanged. Tests with simulated data (`tests/test_paired_resolution.py`): without a true difference the false-positive rate lies in 0.045-0.055 (20 000 simulations each) for n = 3 and n = 5, with a seed effect common to both methods of 0, 1 and 10 times the method noise; agreement with `scipy.stats.ttest_rel` (statistic, p value, confidence interval).

**c) D1 -- planned future inputs (`447f0c9`).** `WindowConfig.future_actions` / `DataSpec.future_actions`: `"realised"` (default, behaviour up to now) or `"planned"` (`Trajectory.requested_actions`, the set points before the gas-velocity projection, which depends on the true grain state). The history inputs stay realised. Same option in the point-split path. Acts only if the process config has `numerics.enforce_gas_velocity_projection` on. The option enters the data fingerprints (`window/future_actions`) only when it is `"planned"`; `process/fingerprint`, `excitation/fingerprint`, `split/digest` and `measurement/digest` of the default data are pinned by a regression test to the values recorded before the change.

**d) E3 -- own disturbance process of the solid fraction (`d2f5d9f`).** `DiurnalDisturbanceDesign(solid_fraction_process=...)` / `DataSpec.solid_fraction_process`: `"diurnal"` (default) or `"independent"` (own Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, no diurnal term). Ambient temperature and humidity are bit-identical for the same seed in both modes. The standard deviation fraction 0.09 is a **placeholder without a source**, chosen so that the within-run standard deviation of the channel matches the old one (ad-hoc measurement, not stored as an artifact: 64 runs of `broadband_derived`, seeds 11-13: 0.0140-0.0146 against 0.0135-0.0145). Within-run correlation with the ambient temperature at seed 11 (same ad-hoc measurement): median 0.03 instead of 0.59 (the review reported 0.71 for its own seed); the median of the absolute correlation is 0.24, because two slow independent processes can correlate by chance over 8 h. The option enters the excitation fingerprint only when it is not `"diurnal"`.

**e) Defaults and preset (`60780ac`).** The defaults of `DataSpec` stay at the old behaviour: about 50 scripts build `DataSpec()` and would silently change their data (for E3 all of them). New studies use only the named preset `DataSpec.new_study(...)` (`future_actions="planned"`, `solid_fraction_process="independent"`; the two options cannot be overridden through it); CLAUDE.md says so.

**f) Where the code is loaded from (`b3c5fdd`, `c5b9f33`).** Finding on the way: the system interpreter's editable install points at the old checkout `../twinlink_ml` (last commit 2026-09-25, no `joint_search`, `site_network`, `line_tables`), not at this repository; the `.venv` of this checkout points here and holds every extra of `pyproject.toml`. New `utils/code_location.py`: every new artifact records `code/package_dir` (relative), `code/interpreter`, `code/root_checked`; if the loaded `twinlink_ml` is not `<root>/src/twinlink_ml` of the repository or worktree the run belongs to, the run aborts (`environment_fingerprint()`: root = repository of the working directory; `scripts/verify/_common.provenance()` and the three `report_partner_*` scripts: root = repository of the script). `tools/run_here.sh` starts a command with the worktree's own code; the protocol is in CLAUDE.md. Review of the past (read only): all JSONL logs since 2026-10-01 carry commits of this repository and numpy 2.5.3 / torch 2.14.0 (the `.venv`); the detached drivers of the K1 re-runs and of M4-R use the `.venv` with `PYTHONPATH` on the worktree `src`; for the JSON artifacts of M3 (2026-10-06/07), M3x and M4-C the loading is not documented in the records. For M3x and M4-C it cannot matter (`src/` did not change between `ef58cf8` and `9dec7cb`); for M3 (Befunde 71, 73) it follows only from the fact that the modules of the joint stage did not exist in master at that time.

**g) Tests.** Full suite in the `.venv` (with gymnasium): **740 passed, 2 skipped** (14 min 45 s) at `c5b9f33`; the two skips are a data-dependent saturation check in `tests/test_bandit_env_shield.py:147` and a test of the error path without torch (`tests/test_experiments.py:317`, torch is installed). With the previous system interpreter 10 tests were skipped, 7 of them because gymnasium was missing (suite at `d2f5d9f`: 676 passed, 10 skipped). The fingerprint regression tests (`tests/test_process_config_fingerprint_regression.py` and the pinned values in `tests/test_future_actions.py`) stayed green throughout.

**h) Open.** Whether and how the older rank statements change under the paired resolution is not part of this entry (separate evaluation, pure re-analysis of committed records, no training). The review items C3, C4 (for the old function), C-L1, C-L2, C-Q1 are unchanged (`docs/12`).

### 83. The rank statements of Befunde 58, 63 and 67 re-evaluated with the paired resolution: the main statements stand; 11 of 92 verdict cells change, among them the Transformer deficit on moisture, which is resolvable again

**a) Status.** Pure re-analysis of committed records (`arch_learning_curve_projected*.jsonl`, `arch_epoch_budget_probe600.jsonl`, `sx3_capacity_matched_a/b.jsonl`), no training, no new data. Script `scripts/analyze_paired_reevaluation.py` (commit `f6d2d23`; rule, cells and the old verdicts used for comparison are fixed in its docstring; a dry run of the identical computation, nothing written, was made before that commit to find script errors; no rule was changed after it), artifact `paired_reevaluation_58_63_67.json` (clean tree, `.venv`, `code/package_dir` `src/twinlink_ml`). **Not yet taken over into the synthesis (`docs/08`) or the register (`docs/12`); for review by the project lead.** The older entries keep their wording.

**b) Method (review C1/C2).** All methods of Befunde 51/58/67 ran with the same `master_seed` set 1-5; the `split/digest` is identical per seed and budget for all methods in all three record sets (20 points checked in the script). The paired test of `evaluation/paired_resolution.py` (`cd7b562`) is applied: differences `reference - candidate` of `rmse_run_median_physical` per seed, h = 36, t distribution with 4 degrees of freedom, two-sided 95 %, **test on the mean of the differences** (the old verdicts compare medians). Sensitivity, never used for the verdict: the same test on `log(candidate / reference)`. "Old" verdict = the final one of the lab book (Welch-t of Befund 67/SX1, `sx1_resolution_t.json`, and `sx3_capacity_matched.json`); the z verdict of Befund 63 g is in the artifact. Befund 58 states no threshold; its statements are mapped to cells and tested for the first time. **632 tests in total, no correction for multiplicity** (docs/12 C-L1 open). Test sets named per cell: excited, constant-run holdout; `n_train = 64` for 63/67, 8/16/32/64 for 58. Unchanged confound (docs/12 F1.4): GRU, LSTM and the baselines were trained on Linux, Transformer, xLSTM, Mamba and all SX3 variants on Windows; a difference between the two groups contains the platform.

**c) Befund 63 and the SX1 addendum (26 distinct cells with an old verdict): 2 change.**

| cell (candidate vs. LSTM, `n_train` 64) | old (z / Welch-t) | new (paired) | median difference | seeds worse | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| moisture, excited, Transformer | resolved / **unresolved** | **resolvably worse** | -98.6 % | 5 of 5 | 0.032 |
| moisture, constant holdout, Transformer | resolved / **unresolved** | **resolvably worse** | -45.9 % | 5 of 5 | 0.012 |

The other 24 cells give the same verdict as the Welch-t verdict of Befund 67: GRU vs. LSTM unresolved in all six cells; Transformer resolvably worse on `energy_target` (excited; constant holdout at 200 and 600 epochs) and on `bed_temperature_celsius` (excited), unresolved on `bed_temperature_celsius` (constant holdout, 200 and 600 epochs; 4 of 5 and 3 of 5 seeds worse, p = 0.30 and 0.66); Mamba resolvably worse in 6 of 6; xLSTM in 4 of 6 (`energy_target`, `bed_temperature_celsius`; on moisture unresolved, p = 0.158 excited and 0.103 constant holdout, although the median differences are -140 % and -114 % and the candidate is worse in 5 of 5 seeds). The log-ratio sensitivity differs in one of these cells (xLSTM, moisture, constant holdout: worse). **Consequence for the wording of Befund 67:** the Transformer deficit on moisture, which the addendum called "no longer resolvable with five seeds", is resolvable in the paired design (all five seeds worse; the log-ratio sensitivity agrees). **e) Befund 58 (432 comparisons on the budget range and 30 pairwise ones, five seeds, no old thresholds).**
- *"GRU/LSTM remain the best trained models over the whole tested budget range":* stands. Of 144 comparisons (Transformer, xLSTM, Mamba against LSTM and against GRU, 4 budgets x 3 channels x 2 test sets) **none** is resolvably in favour of the candidate. Against LSTM: Transformer resolvably worse in 17 of 24 cells, xLSTM in 18, Mamba in 20 (the remainder unresolved).
- *GRU against LSTM at other budgets (Befund 63 checked `n_train` 64 only):* resolvably better for GRU in 4 of 18 cells at `n_train` 8, 16, 32, all five seeds better: `bed_temperature_celsius` excited at 8 (7.6 %), `energy_target` excited at 16 (19.2 %), constant holdout at 16 (10.5 %) and at 32 (9.5 %); none at 64 (as in Befund 63). With 18 uncorrected tests about one false positive is expected; four is more than that, but not a basis for a ranking. The wording "GRU or LSTM" stands for `n_train` 64; at smaller budgets GRU is not behind LSTM.
- *Ordering on moisture (excited, `n_train` 64: LSTM 0.00051 < GRU 0.00061 < Transformer 0.00101 < xLSTM 0.00123 < Mamba 0.00505):* only the ends are resolvable. Resolved: LSTM < Transformer, LSTM < Mamba, GRU < Mamba, Transformer < Mamba, xLSTM < Mamba. Unresolved: LSTM-GRU, LSTM-xLSTM, GRU-Transformer (p = 0.062), GRU-xLSTM, Transformer-xLSTM. The statement "factor 9.9 between best and worst" holds (LSTM vs. Mamba); the order of the middle three is not established.
- *"At small budgets larger models are worse than GRU/LSTM" (moisture, excited, `n_train` 8):* resolvable for the xLSTM against LSTM and GRU and for Mamba against LSTM (p = 0.006) but not against GRU (p = 0.056); **not** for the Transformer (against LSTM p = 0.078, against GRU p = 0.60, although its median is 2.03 times the LSTM's).
- *Catch-up of the Transformer on `bed_temperature_celsius` (constant holdout, h = 36), ratio of the medians to LSTM:* 1.40 / 1.24 / 1.09 / 1.03 at `n_train` 8 / 16 / 32 / 64: resolvably worse at 8, 16 and 32, **unresolved at 64** ("parity" means "no longer distinguishable with five seeds", not a proven equality). xLSTM (6.19, 4.68, 1.92, 1.80) and Mamba (3.90, 3.32, 3.20, 2.46) stay resolvably worse at all four budgets. On moisture (excited) the Transformer's ratio of 2.03 at 8 and 1.99 at 64 is resolvable only at 64.
- *`energy_target`, excited, `n_train` 64, "6.4-7.8 times better than the static regression" (GRU / LSTM / Transformer):* stands in the paired design (ratios of the medians 7.68 / 7.82 / 6.43, all five seeds better, p < 0.001); on the constant holdout 5.74 / 5.62 / 5.20. The xLSTM is resolvably worse than the static regression on both test sets (ratio 0.26, 4 of 5 seeds worse, p = 0.034 and 0.041), Mamba better (2.09 / 2.44).
- *"xLSTM is not better than persistence at small budgets" (`energy_target`, excited):* **not resolvable** at any budget: -9.4 % (8), -16.6 % (16), +5.3 % (32), +12.0 % (64), p = 0.91 / 0.83 / 0.12 / 0.23. Befund 58 compared medians without a threshold; neither the worse-than-persistence at 8 and 16 nor the better-than-persistence at 32 and 64 is established.
- LSTM against the baselines (24 cells each): resolvably better than the static regression in 20, than ARX in 22, than persistence in 20; the unresolved cells lie at `n_train` 8 and 16, mostly on moisture.

**f) What does not change, and what this does not show.** The main message of the three entries stands: GRU and LSTM are the best trained models and are not distinguishable from each other at `n_train` 64; Mamba and the mLSTM-only variants stay behind; the Transformer reaches parity only on bed temperature. Changed are details: the moisture deficit of the Transformer is resolvable, the sLSTM 2-layer variant now formally meets reading C, the comparison of the xLSTM with persistence and the middle of the moisture ordering of Befund 58 are not established, and GRU is resolvably better than LSTM in some cells at smaller budgets. The mean test is weak when one seed diverges (mLSTM, mixed variant): of the 92 distinct cells of Befunde 63/67 with an old verdict, 10 differ between the mean test and the log-ratio sensitivity (1 in Befund 63, 9 in SX3); over all 632 tests 51 differ. The required number of seeds of Befund 63 h ("41 seeds") was **not** recomputed for the paired design; with pairing it will be smaller where the seed effect is shared. Not re-checked: the epoch-cap status per cell, the platform confound, other horizons and channels, Befund 63 a (speed) and the cost statements.

| split | steps limited | runs with a limited step | F windows (legacy) | F windows (N) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| train, 64 runs | 5.9 % / 5.8 % | 18 of 64 / 17 of 64 | 8.8 % | 8.6 % |
| train, first 8 runs (pilot training set) | 6.5 % / 6.7 % | 1 of 8 / 1 of 8 | 8.6 % | 8.8 % |
| validation | 4.9 % / 5.2 % | 6 of 32 / 6 of 32 | 6.2 % | 6.5 % |
| excited test | 7.3 % / 7.5 % | 10 of 32 / 10 of 32 | 9.7 % | 10.2 % |
| constant-run holdout | 10.7 % / 10.4 % | 9 of 32 / 9 of 32 | 10.6 % | 10.2 % |

Windows whose history only contains a limited step: 0.7-1.7 %. - **Test-time part (A0 model on planned instead of realised future inputs, excited):** the squared error is unchanged in the U windows (ratio 1.00, the inputs are identical there) and rises only in the F windows: `energy_target` GRU x175, LSTM x109, Transformer x79, ARX x17.8, static x13.8, Mamba x4.9, xLSTM x0.89; `bed_temperature_celsius` GRU x9.4, LSTM x11.9, Transformer x7.3, ARX x2.2, Mamba x1.2, xLSTM x2.4. In A0 the F windows are the better predicted ones (GRU `energy_target` RMSE 0.035 in F against 0.064 in U; the persistence RMSE is also lower there, 0.49 against 0.71), i.e. the models used the clipped future velocity.

Constant holdout (F 10.6 %): `energy_target` 0.17 / 0.11 / 0.24 / 0.14 (GRU / LSTM / Transformer / Mamba), `bed_temperature_celsius` 0.09-0.36. **The increase is concentrated in the F windows (on `energy_target` four to seven times their share of the windows on the excited set, on `bed_temperature_celsius` one to four times) but it is not almost only there for the trained networks: 35-90 % of it lies in windows without a limited step** (squared-error ratio in the U windows on `energy_target`: GRU x7.3, LSTM x3.2, Transformer x2.1, Mamba x2.2; `bed_temperature_celsius` x1.3-1.7). The static regression and ARX (no learned dependence on the history) rise only in the F windows (U ratio 1.00). Reading: the networks trained on the clipped inputs also lose in the unlimited windows when trained on planned inputs; the mechanism is not identified here (one possibility: a dependence on the clipped velocity learned from the 6 % limited steps carries over to windows that follow them; windows with a limited step only in their history are 1.2-1.7 % and are in U). On moisture the networks do not get systematically worse (ratios below and above 1). **Caveats:** one seed, `n_train` 8 (one of the eight training runs contains limited steps: 595 limited steps), group sizes 424 F windows on the excited test set; the shares are descriptive.

**e) (c) Which part of the excitation requests actions outside the fluidisation window (legacy pool; margins recomputed from the pre-step state; clipping the request with them reproduces the realised action exactly, maximum difference 0).** All 8867 limited steps are above `u_t`; 34 of the 128 runs are affected.
- By signal kind of the gas-velocity channel (runs with a limited step / runs, share of its steps): step 16 / 54 (7.3 %), PRBS 11 / 28 (7.5 %), constant 4 / 13 (7.7 %), ramp 3 / 33 (1.9 %); constant runs 4 of 13, other runs 30 of 115.
- By initial diameter (terciles): 250-383 um: 17.2 % of the steps (29 runs), 386-583 um: 0.8 % (5 runs), 588-896 um: none. By run time (terciles): first third 13.0 %, second 4.4 %, last 0.6 %. **The limit binds for small particles early in a run:** `u_t` grows with the diameter, which grows during the run.
- **Conservative window.** Largest `u_mf` over the pool 0.30 m/s, smallest `u_t` 1.257 m/s (empirical, smallest particle 251 um); the analytic `u_t` at the smallest initial diameter (250.6 um) with the worst bed temperature (29.6-105.9 degC) and inlet humidity (0.0014-0.0305 kg/kg) seen in the pool: **1.230 m/s**. A window `[0.8, 1.23-1.26]` m/s is non-empty but covers 25-27 % of the gas-velocity box (0.8-2.5 m/s); a clip of the request into it would change **76.6 %** of the requested samples. **Re-simulation of the whole pool with the gas-velocity requests clipped: 0 limited steps remain** for the global cap (empirical 1.257 and analytic 1.230 m/s alike). **Run-specific cap** (`u_t` at the run's own initial diameter, worst-case temperature and humidity of the pool; median 2.41 m/s, minimum 1.23, maximum 3.91 m/s; no cap below the box minimum): changes the requests of 44 of 128 runs and 19.4 % of the requested samples, and the re-simulation again has **0 limited steps**. So a conservatively limited excitation window is possible; the global form costs three quarters of the gas-velocity range, the run-specific form (which needs the initial particle size of a run, a design quantity of the simulation) about a fifth of the samples. Not examined: the effect on the learned dynamics, the effect on the high-velocity regime (above `u_t` the model has no entrainment term, Befund 46, so these are not valid operating points of the model), other seeds, the distribution of the initial diameter.

### 86. Decision: the preset for new studies caps the gas velocity per run at the terminal velocity of its initial diameter (preset version 2); the projection stays on as a counted guard; arm N of the re-run is redefined accordingly

**a) Decision of the project lead (2026-10-13), valid for all new studies.** `DataSpec.new_study()` gets a **per-run limit of the requested gas velocity: every run requests at most the terminal velocity `u_t` at its INITIAL diameter.** The gas-velocity projection stays on as a guard; how often it acts is counted per pool (expected: never). The preset gets a **version number** that enters the data fingerprints, every record and the provenance block of every artifact. `DataSpec()` is unchanged (old data and fingerprints reproduce). Studies A and B merge `master` into their branches once this is pushed.

**b) Reasons.** (1) The operator knows the starting material of a run; the initial diameter is a quantity of the design, so the limit needs no knowledge of the state during the run. (2) The particles grow during the run, so `u_t` only rises: a request at most `u_t(d_0)` never leaves the fluidisation window at the upper side. (3) The alternative, one global limit for all runs, would lose three quarters of the gas-velocity range (Befund 85 e: `u_t` at the smallest initial diameter 1.23 m/s against the box 0.8-2.5 m/s, a window of 25-27 % of the box, 76.6 % of the requested samples changed); the per-run limit changes the requests of 44 of 128 runs and 19.4 % of the requested samples (same entry, seed 1). The numbers of Befund 85 behind it, legacy pool seed 1: 8867 limited steps (6.0 %), all above `u_t`, 34 of 128 runs, 5.9-10.7 % of the steps by split, binding for small particles early in a run (17.2 % of the steps in the smallest tercile of the initial diameter, none in the largest).

**c) What was implemented (commit `87031be`).** `gas_velocity_cap_from_initial_diameter` (`simulation/excitation.py`): `u_t` at the run's initial diameter, **minimum over the whole a-priori range** of the bed temperature (smallest ambient temperature to the largest inlet temperature of the action space) and of the inlet humidity (corners of the ambient ranges), 9 x 9 grid, never below the box minimum; applied by `MixedExcitationDesign(gas=..., gas_velocity_cap="initial_diameter")` as a minimum with a constant per run, so the rate limit of the signal is kept. Unlike the analysis of Befund 85 (which used the ranges seen in the pool) the limit uses a-priori ranges only. `DataSpec.gas_velocity_cap` (default `"none"`) and `DataSpec.new_study_version` (default `None`); `NEW_STUDY_PRESET_VERSION = 2` (version 1 = planned future inputs + own solid-fraction process, the pilot arm N of Befund 84; version 2 = + the per-run limit). `GeneratedData.projection_guard` counts projected steps and runs per pool; the re-run worker logs it for the training/test pool and the holdout pool in every record (`pool/projected_steps`, `holdout_pool/projected_steps`, ...). The version goes into the excitation fingerprint only when the limit is set, into `preset/new_study_version` of the data fingerprints, into `data/new_study_version` of every record and into `preset/new_study_version` of `environment_fingerprint()` and of the provenance block of the scripts. Old fingerprints are unchanged (regression tests of Befunde 82 and the new tests).

**d) Tests and check.** `tests/test_gas_velocity_cap.py`: a re-simulated pool (16 runs of 8 h) and a constant-run holdout built with the limit have **zero** limited steps, while the legacy pools with the same seeds have many (the test fails if the legacy pool is not limited); every request is at most its run's limit; all other channels, the disturbances and the initial states are identical to the unlimited schedule of the same seed; the rate limit of the gas velocity holds; the excitation fingerprint changes only when the limit is set and equals that of a design built without the new arguments otherwise; the version appears in the fingerprints only for the preset. Ad-hoc check (not stored as an artifact) on the full re-run pools with the preset (128 runs, seeds 1-5; `generate_data`, projection on): **0 projected steps in each of the five pools** (147 456 steps each) and **0 in the constant-run holdout pool of seed 999** (41 472 steps), against 8867 projected steps in 34 runs for the legacy pool of seed 1; limits per run: minimum 1.22-1.23 m/s, median 2.37-2.38 m/s, maximum 3.78-3.79 m/s. The counts of the real runs are in the records (`pool/projected_steps`); a count above 0 there is to be reported, not assumed away.

**e) What this changes for older work.** The old data (`DataSpec()`) were produced with the projection acting in 2-7 % of the steps in some pools (legacy pool seed 1: 6.0 %). **Study B has so far run without the projection** (statement of the project lead); its trajectories were therefore at 2-7 % of the steps above the terminal velocity, i.e. outside the validity of the model (Befund 46: no entrainment term above `u_t`). Not checked here; it concerns the data of study B, not the repository. Effect on the learned dynamics of the limit is not examined (Befund 85 e).

**f) Re-run.** Arm A1 stays as planned (legacy trajectories, planned future inputs: measures how much the old findings profited from the information leak). **Arm N is redefined as the preset version 2** (planned inputs, own solid-fraction process, per-run limit), the basis of the synthesis, version 5; the pilot arm N (version 1) is a pilot only. `docs/15` is changed accordingly before any computation. The full run starts when the main runs of studies A and B have finished, then with all 16 workers: about 113 core-hours of committed timings (A1 8 and 64, N 8-64, five seeds) is about 7 h ideal, about 11-14 h with the margin of the plan.

Full suite at `87031be`: **767 passed, 2 skipped** (19 min 20 s); pushed.

### 87. Study B1 (information per run, active learning): equal-cost excitation plans B0-B4, test sets T1-T3, growing pool and a run-time pilot at N = 4 -- built and tested; no main run, no result

**a) Scope.** Study B1 of the project lead (2026-10-12): which excitation yields the most information per run, and does active learning save runs? This entry records the build and the pilot only. The main run is drafted in `docs/16_draft_b1_main_run.md` (not released). Branch `b1-excitation-active-learning`, worktree `C:	winlink_work1`, not pushed, not merged. New modules only; no shared file changed (`excitation.py`, `generate_data` and the config schema are untouched).

**b) What was built** (`simulation/excitation_plans.py`, `simulation/excitation_information.py`, `evaluation/growing_pool.py`, `evaluation/b1_testsets.py`, tests `tests/test_b1_*.py`).
- Plans B0 constant, B1 random steps (the previous design with `constant_run_fraction = 0`), B2 two-scale multi-level PRBS, B3 multisine with Schroeder phases, B4 space-filling set points with holds. Equal cost by construction: the same disturbance and initial-state draw (bit-identical per seed), the same bounds and rate limits (`check_equal_cost`, tested).
- Time constants are the measured ones (Befund 3, addendum M1), not the rules of thumb of the task text: fast mode 30.2-38.8 s, coupled slow mode 133.5-1194.9 s, solids loop 600 s, residence 16000 s (not excitable within a run, covered by the initial states). Derived: B2 clocks 75 s and 900 s, B3 band 1.3e-4 to 5.3e-3 Hz, B4 hold 2400 s with 12 holds per run (the longest hold with at least twice the slowest coupled time constant and an integer number of holds per run). Deviation from the task text (15-80 s and about 600 s): the fast mode starts at 30 s, the slow coupled mode reaches 1195 s at the cold end.
- Model-free measures: spectral coverage of the measured band, Fisher information of an input-only FIR regression (usable before a run), Fisher information of the ARX regression (needs outputs, analysis only).
- Growing pool: candidate plans are inputs only; the truth of a run exists only after `add`. The full pool built in chunks is bit-identical to `generate_data` (test `test_full_pool_equals_generate_data`). Sensor noise of the pool is drawn per run (the batch stream of `rollout` depends on the batch composition); the batch stream is reproduced only for that test.
- Test sets: T1 neutral mix of B0-B4, T2 constant operation, T3 deployment profiles (start in a steady state, one hour hold, four set-point changes of two channels by 5-10 % of their span). Test seeds come from a fixed namespace; every test run is checked against the training runs (ids and action arrays).

**c) T3 anchors** (artifact `b1_t3_anchors`, script commit `4eccb3e`, clean tree, `.venv`): constrained optimum of the `energy_target` objective at four ambient conditions (quartiles of the disturbance ranges), lower gas-velocity bound 1.26 m/s, quality limit 0.15 kg/kg (decoupled field), search of Befund 52 (DE popsize 10, maxiter 50, seed 0, Nelder-Mead, precision 30 / 1e-7), corrected solver bracket. Wall time 364 s with four workers. The optimum sits on the lower bound of the inlet temperature (60 degC at three points) and of the nozzle pressure (about 1.0 bar), and at three of the four ambient points the steady-state moisture equals the limit (0.1500); the second T3 anchor (half the M1 margin below the limit, found by bisection on the spray rate) therefore differs from the optimum by about 1 % of the spray rate at those points. Open decision O1 of the draft.

**d) Pilot** (artifact `pilot_b1_b2_n4`, script commit `4eccb3e`, clean tree, `.venv`, 8 worker processes with one thread each): B1 and B2 at N = 4 runs, five seeds (the same for both designs), persistence, ARX and LSTM, test sets T1 (40 runs), T2 (32), T3 (32), `ValidationPolicy.NONE`. Purpose: run times. Wall time of the ten jobs 331.7 s; LSTM fit 70-79 s per job while eight jobs ran concurrently, 40-42 s when two ran; data generation for four runs 7.7-8.7 s; build of the three test sets 50 s. **Addendum 5 (2026-10-13): descriptive analysis of the main run (no new hypotheses): information measures against errors, what the data exclude, run equivalents, secondary targets and horizon 1.** Script and module (`scripts/analyze_b1_descriptive.py`, `evaluation/b1_descriptive.py`, tests) committed before the run (`2be7b7f`; attempt 1 artifact `b1_descriptive_analysis` kept as a record, its bootstrap percentiles are NaN where resamples have infinite run equivalents; fixed and rerun: `71fe997`); result artifact **`b1_descriptive_analysis_2`** (clean tree, `git/dirty = False`, same ten seeds and 1440 records as Addendum 4, 1000 bootstrap resamples over the seeds). Primary quantity as before: LSTM, product moisture, horizon 24, run-median RMSE; intervals are paired 95 % intervals (t, 9 degrees of freedom) of the mean difference, no multiplicity correction, in percent of the mean error of the reference, positive = the candidate is better. (1) **Do the information measures explain the order of the excitations? Partly, and only for the LSTM.** Rank correlation of the measure of a pool with the error, per N, test set and model; arm level = mean measure over the seeds against the median error (one point per arm), seed level = one point per arm and seed pooled within N (expected sign negative for information, positive for `fir_condition`, `arx_condition`, `max_abs_cross_correlation`). *With B0 (five arms B0-B4)* every information measure orders the arms as the LSTM error does on all three test sets (arm-level Spearman -0.9 to -1.0 at N = 4-32 on T1 and T3, -0.7 to -0.9 on T2; FIR and ARX log-determinant, smallest eigenvalue and spectral coverage at 1, 10 and 25 % behave alike); this is driven by B0, which has the least information and by far the largest error. *Without B0 (B1-B4, B5, B5r, six arms; a coarse test, |rho| of about 0.83 is needed for p < 0.05)*: LSTM, FIR log-determinant per parameter, arm level N = 4 / 8 / 16 / 32: T1 -0.89 / -0.83 / -0.94 / -0.94, T3 -0.60 / -0.60 / -0.60 / -0.77, T2 +0.03 / -0.49 / -0.54 / -0.37; seed level T1 -0.66 to -0.81, T3 -0.2 to -0.4, T2 -0.26 to -0.38; ARX log-determinant and spectral coverage give the same picture (T1 -0.9, T3 -0.6, T2 about -0.5, spectral coverage somewhat lower). At N = 2 the correlations are near 0 or positive (B5 and B5r share the start pool). So among the excited designs more Fisher information goes with a lower LSTM error on T1 and, more weakly, on T3, and not clearly on T2. **For the ARX the sign is the opposite or absent** (excited arms, arm level: T2 +0.3 to +0.9, T3 +0.3 to +0.9, T1 about 0), i.e. the measures do not explain the order of the ARX errors. `max_abs_cross_correlation` has the wrong sign among B0-B4 (-0.3 to -0.9 instead of positive) because the constant B0 has zero variance and so zero cross-correlation by construction; among the excited arms it is weakly positive for the LSTM (+0.1 to +0.8). The three coverage thresholds (1, 10, 25 %) rank the arms nearly alike and are no better than the FIR information. Not shown: that the measures cause the differences (six arms, pools of one design type each). (2) **What the data exclude** (LSTM, moisture, h = 24; "differences larger than X % are excluded" = the larger absolute bound of the interval). *T3, B2 against B1:* N = 4 interval -9 to +68 % (an improvement larger than 68 % or a deterioration larger than 9 % is excluded), N = 8 -11 to +42 %, N = 16 +2 to +51 %, N = 32 -4 to +25 %. *T3, B3 against B1:* N = 4 -86 to +43 %, N = 8 -56 to +27 %, N = 32 -36 to +4 % (B3 is not better than B1 by more than 4 % at N = 32; worse by up to 36 %). *T3, B4 against B1:* -12 to +50 % (N = 4), -47 to +23 % (8), -13 to +40 % (16), -14 to +25 % (32). *T3, B5 against B1:* -62 to +51 % (4), -61 to +17 % (8), -8 to +45 % (16), -2 to +28 % (32). *T3, B5 against B5r:* -39 to +77 % (4), -70 to +10 % (8), +2 to +26 % (16, resolved), -4 to +24 % (32). *T1, B2 against B1:* +9 to +98 % (4), +23 to +63 % (8), +21 to +39 % (16), +7 to +22 % (32), i.e. B2 is resolved better on T1 at every N from 2; B3 is resolved worse at N = 16 and 32 (-55 to -30 %, -59 to -33 %); B5 against B5r on T1 is resolved worse at N = 8 (-83 to -9 %). *T2, B2 against B1:* -1 to +103 % (4), +19 to +61 % (8), +13 to +39 % (16), -12 to +39 % (32). In words: on T3 at N = 4 the data allow no difference between B2 and B1 larger than 68 % in B2's favour or 9 % in B1's favour; at N = 32 no difference larger than 25 % in favour of B2 or B4, none larger than 28 % in favour of B5 and none larger than 4 % in favour of B3 over B1 on T3; the intervals are wide at N = 2-8 (several tens of percent) and narrow only at N >= 16. All run equivalents rest on medians of ten seeds and on the interpolation of a five-point curve.
