The statement of Addendum 4 (B2 about as good as or better than the others, B5 not better than B5r) therefore holds on the secondary targets too; the long horizon is where the excitations differ. (5) **Reservation: the gas-velocity limit.** Under preset version 2 the gas velocity sits on its per-run limit (the terminal velocity at the initial diameter) in **20-24 % of the steps of every plan** (Addendum 3, artifact `b1_pool_limits`: B0 21.2 %, B1 21.7 %, B2 24.0 %, B3 19.6 %, B4 21.7 %). That can have made the excitations more alike in this channel and so **reduced the differences between them** (a plan that would have excited the gas velocity above the limit is clipped to the same level as the others), and the information measures were computed on the limited requests. The size of the effect was not measured: this study has no run without the limit (the pilot ran without it, at N = 4 only and for B1 and B2). The rate limiter shapes the plans unequally (B2: 18 % of the inlet-temperature and 35 % of the spray-rate steps against none for B0 and B3) and is part of what each plan is. Merged into `master` as Befund 87 (2026-10-14; `docs/16` keeps its number). **Independently recomputed** by a second, separate implementation of the same evaluation (branch `b1-descriptive-eval`, not merged, archived as tag `archive/b1-descriptive-eval`): the results agree. **Added reservation: T1 contains test runs of the plan an arm was trained on (eight runs of each of B0-B4), a possible home advantage of the plan's own arm; T3 is free of it.** Statements that rest on T1 (for example B2 resolved better than B1 at all five N on T1) are to be read with that reservation.


### 88. Study A1, main run: the value of a simulator for a data-poor LSTM on a structurally different plant -- pretraining + fine-tuning beats "from scratch" at small N on every plant (HA1 supported, crossover not reached on four of five plants) and is never worse (HA2 not supported); the hybrid is never better than pretraining + fine-tuning (HA3 not supported); the simulator channel costs about 100 times the network at inference (for review, not yet in the synthesis or the register)

**a) Question and design.** How much does a simulator help a data-poor model when the plant is structurally different from it, and from how many plant runs on does it no longer help? Plants as separate classes behind the simulator interface (`simulation/plant_variants.py`): P0 (identical), P1 (parameters: heat loss x1.30, gas-solid transfer x0.75 -- a PROXY via `max_saturation_degree`, the model has no heat-transfer coefficient --, critical moisture x1.20 for the kinetics only, the quality limit pinned), P2a (kinetics only: drying curve eta^2, an exact option `MaterialConfig.drying_curve_exponent`), P2b (measurement only: lag, dead time, offset between bed and exhaust), P3 (P2a + P2b + fouling within a run, restarting with every run). Five seeds, N = 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 plant runs, one LSTM (hidden 64, one layer, three targets: energy target, product moisture, bed temperature; NOT the per-target composite of Befund 26, which has no `fine_tune`), horizon 36 (900 s). Methods: from scratch (4000 gradient steps), pretraining + fine-tuning (one pretrained model per seed on P0 data, 256 + 32 runs; all parameters, learning rate 3e-4, 320 epochs, pretraining scalers kept), hybrid (the open P0 simulation -- noise-free measurement of P0, started in the steady state at the set points of the run, inputs only -- as three more exogenous channels; 16000 steps), the simulator alone, persistence, ARX; a sensitivity of the hybrid with 8000 steps at N = 2 and 4. Data only with `DataSpec.new_study` preset version 2 (Befund 86). Per plant and seed a pool of 128 runs (64 train, 32 reserved validation runs in no fit, 32 test runs) and a fixed pool of 16 constant-run test runs. Test sets named: PRIMARY the 32 excited test runs of the plant's own pool, SECONDARY the constant-run holdout (reported apart, never pooled). Metric: median over test runs of the RMSE in physical units at h = 36 per channel; learning curves with median and range over the seeds.

**b) How the settings were fixed (pilots only on the pilot plants PP and PP2, which are not in the main run).** The settings come from two pilots and a confirmation, each with its rule written before the run. Pilot 1 (`a1_pilot_pp.json`, script `46998d6`): selected learning rate 1e-4 and 5 epochs, the EDGE of its grid. Pilot 2 on PP (summary deviation from P0 0.13) and PP2 (0.30), selection by the lowest mean criterion C over both plants, grid extended upward until the selection was interior (`a1_pilot2_pp_pp2.json`, script `765c233`): all parameters trained, learning rate 3e-4, 320 epochs (C 0.0771; 640 epochs 0.0800, 160 epochs 0.0774); step budgets 4000 for "from scratch" (its own optimum), 8000 for the hybrid. The excitation of all studies was then changed (Befund 86, preset version 2) and the settings were confirmed on the new data (`a1_confirm_preset2.json`, script `f382272`; rule: a chosen setting stays if its mean C is at most 3 % above the best tested): fine-tuning stays (C 0.0510 against 0.0499 for 1e-4 / 640 epochs, +2.1 %), "from scratch" stays (4000 steps, C 0.2471 against 0.2841 for 8000), the hybrid does NOT (8000 steps, C 0.2527 against 0.2235 for 16000, +13.0 %). Decision of the project lead: each method at its best tested budget, so the hybrid got **16000 steps. 16000 is the EDGE of the tested range, and the selection is driven by the strongly scattering N = 2 cells** (at N = 2 the C of one setting ranges from 0.13 to 1.05 across three pools; at N = 16 the two hybrid budgets differ by less than the scatter, PP 0.0264 against 0.0270, PP2 0.0261 against 0.0253). Pretraining on data of preset version 2 reached C = 0.0169 on 224 P0 test runs (132 epochs), against 0.0535 on the data of version 1 (31 epochs; different data and test runs, so not one model on one test set); in the main run the five pretrained models reach C = 0.0151-0.0184 (41 to 175 epochs).

**c) The run (`a1_main_records.json`, script `3b78ef1`, clean tree, `.venv`, 8 workers, a worktree on `C:\`, run beside the main run of Study B).** 105 units, 1400 result records, 37 874 s of wall time. Guard: every record carries `data/new_study_version` = 2, and **0 projected steps in every pool** (excited and constant-run pools of all 25 plant-seed combinations, and the five pretraining pools). The steady-state solver of the hybrid channel failed (nominal start) for 200 of 4000 runs (5.0 %); the simulator's own projection acted at 5435 of 4 608 000 samples (0.12 %). All times in the records are marked `timing_context` (parallel load) and are NOT results.

**d) Hypotheses (rules of `docs/17_a1_transfer_main_run_design.md`, paired resolution over the five seeds, 2640 paired tests in total, no multiplicity correction; `a1_main_analysis.json`, script `15782b4`).** *HA1 supported:* on P0 and P1 pretraining + fine-tuning is better than from scratch in 2 of 3 channels at N = 2 and at N = 4; the ratio RMSE(from scratch) / RMSE(pretraining + fine-tuning) (median over seeds, mean over channels) falls from 12.69 (P0) and 10.27 (P1) at N = 2 to 1.32 and 1.27 at N = 64. Crossover N* of pretraining against from scratch: **not reached** on P0, P1, P2a and P2b (still resolved better at N = 64); on P3 it is no longer resolved better from N = 8 (last resolved at N = 4). *HA2 not supported:* pretraining + fine-tuning is not resolved worse than from scratch at any N on any plant, P3 and P2a included (the same on the constant-run holdout). *HA3 not supported:* the hybrid is not better than each of the other three methods in 2 of 3 channels at any of the small N (2, 4, 8, 16) on any of the three structural plants (counts of small N: 0, 0, 0); against pretraining + fine-tuning it is resolved better in 1 of the 90 (plant, N, channel) cells (bed temperature, P3, N = 32) and resolved worse in 34 of the 90, never better in 2 of 3 channels at any N, and resolved worse in 2 of 3 channels on P0 at N = 2, 4, 16, on P1 and P2a at N = 2, 4, 8, 16, on P2b at N = 4 and on P3 at N = 2. Descriptively: the hybrid is resolved better than from scratch in 2 of 3 channels from N = 16 on P0, P2b and P3 and from N = 32 on P1 and P2a; against the simulator alone it is resolved worse at N = 2 and 4 on P0 and at N = 2 on P1 and P2a. Wrong physics against wrong measurement (the separation of P2a and P2b): on P2a (moisture, h = 36, N = 2, median over seeds) the simulator alone is far off (0.0364 kg/kg) and pretraining + fine-tuning is best (0.0040; from scratch 0.0088, hybrid 0.0087); on P2b the simulator alone is best on moisture at N = 2 (0.0051; fine-tuning 0.0059, hybrid 0.0090, from scratch 0.0102) and the hybrid at N = 8 (0.0012 against 0.0013 for fine-tuning), while fine-tuning is best on the bed temperature at N = 2 and 8. The simulator alone is as good as pretraining + fine-tuning on P0 at N = 2 (energy target 0.012 against 0.0143, bed temperature 0.461 against 0.454). Baseline rule (a method is useful only where it beats persistence AND ARX in 2 of 3 channels): useful in 29 of 30 (plant, N) cells for pretraining + fine-tuning, 25 of 30 for from scratch, 24 of 30 for the hybrid; the cells where it fails are in the artifact.

**e) Descriptive additions (no hypothesis of their own).** (1) *Hybrid budget* (8000 against 16000 steps at N = 2 and 4): no conclusion about the hypotheses depends on it -- HA3 is not supported with either (0, 0, 0 small N on all three structural plants); of 90 verdict cells of the hybrid against the other methods 12 differ (7 unresolved -> better, 2 unresolved -> worse, 3 worse -> unresolved); directly, the 8000-step hybrid against the 16000-step one is unresolved in all 15 plant-channel cells at N = 2 and resolved better in 5 of 15 at N = 4. (2) *Nominal start of 200 of 4000 runs:* per seed 6-10 of the 128 runs of the pool (constant-run pool: 1 of 32), 2-3 of the 32 test runs of every seed (1 of the 16 constant-run test runs); in the training prefix only seed 1 has such a run at N <= 16 (position 0). The PRE-REGISTERED comparison ("clean" seeds: none in the training prefix and none among the test runs) therefore has **no clean seed and no comparable cell**. POST HOC (`a1_fallback_training_side.json`): without the test condition, on the seeds 2-5 (four seeds) at N = 2, 4, 8, 16, 180 cells compared; 31 verdicts differ (16 unresolved -> worse, 8 worse -> unresolved, 6 unresolved -> better, 1 better -> unresolved), **no direction flips**, HA3 not supported on the subset either. The effect of the 2-3 nominal-start runs among the test runs cannot be separated (per-run values and the trained models were not kept; the median over the test runs limits their influence); a retraining without these runs was not done.

**f) Inference time (one thread, warm-up excluded; two measurements, both taken while foreign processes ran beside -- NOT on an idle machine).** `a1_inference_time_1thread.json` (script `130b464`; one foreign process at about 1.25 cores) and `a1_inference_time_v2_background.json` (script `4589faa`; machine load 23 % at the start, two foreign processes at about 1.25 cores each), P0 seed 1, 4352 test windows: microseconds per window in a batch / per call with one window (first measurement, second in brackets): persistence 0.1 / 2 (0.2 / 3), simulator alone 0.6 / 5 (0.7 / 7), ARX 2.9 / 159 (4.0 / 262), from scratch 18.0 / 2130 (20.8 / 2220), pretraining + fine-tuning 17.0 / 2110 (20.4 / 3498), hybrid NETWORK only 17.5 / 2108 (21.4 / 2867). The two measurements differ by up to 66 % for the same method; the differences between the three LSTM methods are within that. **The hybrid also needs the simulator channel over the horizon**: in the second measurement the 36 steps of one horizon take 228 993 us for one prediction (min 207 932), so the hybrid costs **231 860 us per prediction in real time (network 2867 us, simulation 98.8 %)**; batched over all test windows the simulation costs 232.1 us per window against 21.4 us for the network (253.5 us in total); with the channel computed for the planned inputs of a whole run in advance (8.87 s per 8 h run, one prediction per sample) 7700 us per prediction are added to the network's 2867 us (10 567 us in total); one simulator step takes 7284 us, the steady-state start of a run 0.28 s. The hybrid is therefore about two orders of magnitude more expensive per prediction than the pure LSTM methods, while the sample time of the plant is 25 s. Repeat on an idle machine: pending (see the addendum).

**g) What is not concluded.** HA3 not supported does not say that the hybrid is useless: it is resolved better than from scratch from N = 16 (P0, P2b, P3) or N = 32 (P1, P2a), but never better than pretraining + fine-tuning, which at small N carries the information of 256 simulated runs while the hybrid, a network trained only on the N plant runs, did not use the simulator channel to the same effect at N = 2 and 4. The statements hold for ONE LSTM over three targets, for the settings fixed on two pilot plants (PP, PP2) and confirmed with a 3 % rule whose hybrid part failed and was resolved by the project lead's decision (16000 steps, the edge of the tested range, driven by N = 2 cells), for five seeds (four degrees of freedom; a resolved difference needs a clear effect, "unresolved" is not "no difference"), and for plants that are variants of the same grey-box model. The deviation of the main variants from P0 is in the pilot artifacts (summary 0.285 P1, 0.305 P2a, 0.312 P3 for the process, 0.405 P3 for the measurement, 0.128 P2b for the measurement; version-1 data), not re-measured on version 2 for them. Nothing here uses the times of the run.

### 90. Heat recovery of the pre-heating stages, partner model v4.1 against an independent counter-current calculation: the partner model recovers 46 to 65 % of it at the sheet's flows; the flow arrangement (equal outlet temperatures = parallel flow) is the assumption that matters; the optimum medium flow is about 25 kg/h with counter-current exchangers, the highest flow in the partner model

Branch `waermerueckgewinnung-vergleich` (merged into `master` on 2026-10-15 as Befund 90). Full text, tables and caveats: `docs/11_partner_model_v4.md`, section 10, written so that it can go to the partner as feedback. Script `scripts/report_heat_recovery_comparison.py` (commit `d3cba2c`), tests `tests/test_heat_recovery_comparison.py` (39), artifact `artifacts/runs/heat_recovery_comparison_r2.json` (`git/dirty=False`); the first run `heat_recovery_comparison.json` (commit `d38f63b`) has identical numbers and only a wrong label of one check (a stage that cools the gas was called a second-law violation). Model against model, no plant data, no change in `src/`, the process configuration default (solid fraction 0.3) untouched (0.40 used as a run parameter for the laboratory-model exhaust of dryer 2).

**a) The heat-network module cannot represent the intermediate circuit** (stage = direct source -> sink pair, no medium in `HeatNetworkConfig`); the circuit was rebuilt in the script. Checks: direct exchange equals `evaluate_cascade` to 3.8e-13 kW, the circuit at `dT_min` 0 equals `partner_v4_1.loops` to 2.5e-10 W. `dT_min` is taken as the approach through the circuit (module convention, `dT_min / 2` per exchanger); the other reading is in the artifact; to be confirmed by the project lead.

**b) Consistency of the partner model (WU0b), v4.1 at 20 kg/h:** energy balances closed (4.5e-13 W; 2.7e-15 on Excel's own cells), no second-law violation, no stage cools the gas, no exhaust below its dew point, total recovery 28.6 / 35.3 / 39.9 % of the pinch target (scenarios 1, 3, 5). Findings: the heat transfer medium leaves at 102.6 degC (scenarios 1-4) and 107.1 degC (5, 6), above 100 degC with `cp` of water; the sheet's gas rows are 108.911 times too high (known). At 150 kg/h per circuit a stage cools the gas (-0.0012 kW, scenarios 3, 4). Positive control: the known -0.0563 kW stage of the intermediate version is found.

**c) Recovered heat (WU1, kW, circuits 20 kg/h, source variant (i), scenario 1 / 3 / 5):** partner 1.777 / 1.420 / 1.606; counter-current with condensation 3.195 / 2.325 / 2.477 (`dT_min` 20 K), 3.662 / 2.559 / 2.751 (10 K), 3.895 / 2.675 / 2.888 (5 K); pinch target at 10 K 4.666 / 3.098 / 3.098. The ranking flow arrangement >> approach > `c_p`, condensation is the same in both orders; at 20 K nothing condenses.

### 91. Storage A1 of plant A (S1): a mixed-node model with both loop orders as a switch; the storage volume is only bounded (about 30 m3 at most), the compressor heat is unmeasured, and the model is not a predictor -- usable for S2 only as a scenario band

Details, tables and the placeholder list: `docs/18_storage_plant_a.md`. Code `src/twinlink_ml/storage_a1/`; script `scripts/study_storage_a1.py` (commit `c9517dc`, run on `191a227`, clean tree, `.venv`); artifact `artifacts/runs/study_storage_a1.json`. Raw data (two 24 h exports, "product 1" and "product 2") stay in `local/`; channel assignment in the git-ignored `conf/plant/plant_local.yaml`; code and docs name roles only.

**a) Model.** Storage A1 as one mixed node; exchanger A1 and the preheater as counter-current effectiveness-NTU exchangers, one conductance each, chain solved in closed form (no iteration); the minimum approach along the exchanger is a check (infeasible state flagged, not capped); steam heat reconstructed from the air balance (`Q_air = Q_out + Q_steam`, fan heat booked). The order in the storage loop is not settled (two control-system pictures disagree): `topology` = B (storage, then exchanger; hot side = storage temperature) or A (exchanger, then storage). Placeholders (volume, storage loss, `T_S,max`, boiler efficiency, fan heat fraction, intake humidity, approach floor, compressor totals) are in the config, in its fingerprint and in `PLACEHOLDERS`; the single storage sensor in the exports means the one-node assumption (three sensors within 0.1 K on two snapshot days, stated by the project lead) is an assumption, not a finding.

**b) Identifiability.** `Q_in` into the storage loop is not measured; the balance `Q_in = rho V c_p dT_S/dt + Q_out + loss` fixes it only up to `V` (same for A and B). `0 <= Q_in <= 1200 kW` gives UPPER bounds on `V` only: 29-32 m3 (product 1) and 57-58 m3 (product 2) for 1-30 min smoothing, both days together **at most about 30 m3**, no lower bound; looser smoothing gives looser bounds (52-75 / 97-169 m3 at 60-120 min). The 1200 kW limit is never binding (at least 466 m3). Reconstructed `Q_in` stays below 470 kW for every admissible `V` (product 2 peaks above the partner's "up to about 400 kW used"). `UA_S` is not identifiable (changes the bound by at most +21 % for 0-2 kW/K). Conductances: exchanger A1 determinable per day for B (19.5 / 25.2 kW/K, +29 % between the days), `V`-dependent for A (13.3 / 15.7); preheater 17.3 / 18.9 kW/K but ill-conditioned above effectiveness 0.85 (product 2). A against B is not decided (weak lean to A: smaller within-day spread and smaller day-to-day change of the implied conductance, `V <= 20 m3`).

**c) Calibration and validation (by day, 24 h).** Preheater supply temperature, validation RMSE 0.86 / 0.55 K (max 3.1 / 2.1 K; persistence 3.3 / 3.2 K). `Q_out` RMSE 96 / 63 kW (max 153 / 89 kW), against persistence 80 / 24 kW: the model does NOT beat persistence for `Q_out` and the steam share (RMSE 0.14 / 0.07 against 0.11 / 0.03) when the days are exchanged. In-sample product 2 does not fit with one preheater conductance either (`Q_out` RMSE 62 kW, return temperature 3.4 K). Storage temperature, 24 h rollout from the initial state with constant `Q_in` (V = 10 m3): 5.5 / 6.3 K RMSE (max 8.7 / 9.7 K), worse than persistence (4.2 / 3.5 K); with `Q_in` reconstructed from the validation day (an oracle, not a prediction) still 7-15 K. ARX baseline: no better, unstable in free run when trained on product 2. One sample of the preheater-loop flow (product 2) dropped to half for one minute; repaired by interpolation, no effect on the fits.

**d) Daily balance (reconstruction, bands over placeholders).** Product 1: heating demand 20 467 kWh/d (mean 852 kW), waste-heat share 32.5 % (30.8-33.2), steam share 67.5 %, CO2 3 084 kg/d (2 698-3 765) against 4 571 without recovery. Product 2: 16 748 kWh/d (697 kW), waste heat 55.6 % (52.0-56.9), steam 44.4 %, CO2 1 663 kg/d (1 415-2 160) against 3 740. CO2 factor: project gas factor 0.201 kg/kWh ("PLH" read as placeholder).

**e) Not concluded / recommendation.** No statement about the real storage volume, the compressor heat, or which loop order is right. The model is not a predictor of the storage temperature or of `Q_out` across days; for S2 it is usable only as a scenario band with every number labelled. Open questions for the partner: compressor heat into the storage loop and the share rejected over the cooler; storage volume; loop order; steam flow or gas consumption and boiler efficiency; air flow through the preheater and intake humidity; the role of the auxiliary air heater.

**f) Files.** `src/twinlink_ml/storage_a1/{config,model,roles,identifiability,calibration,balance}.py`, `tests/test_storage_a1.py` (includes a test that no measurement-point or equipment codes appear in the new files), `conf/plant/plant_local.yaml.example`, `scripts/study_storage_a1.py`, `docs/18_storage_plant_a.md`.

### 92. Shifting potential of storage A1 (S2, scenario band): the pre-registered gate reads L1 by the letter, but the saving is the added compressor heat itself -- pure shifting saves nothing, and a plain rule (logged flow plus taking the discarded heat) captures the optimum (post-hoc L2)

Details, the full table, sensitivity and questions for the partner: `docs/18_storage_plant_a.md`, section 9. Pre-registration: docstring of `scripts/gate_storage_shift.py` (commit `191a227`, committed before the run); artifact `artifacts/runs/gate_storage_shift.json` (run on `790cbba`, clean tree); post-hoc analysis `scripts/analyze_gate_storage_shift.py` and `artifacts/runs/gate_storage_shift_posthoc.json` (declared post-hoc, written after the gate result). **All numbers are scenario numbers (placeholders: discarded compressor heat, storage volume, `T_S,max`, exchanger conductances), not plant statements; the S1 verdict stands (the model is not a predictor).**

**a) Design.** Policies on one discrete model (5 min): R0 replay of the logged preheater-loop flow, R1 rule (maximum flow while `T_S > T_S,min`; takes all discarded heat that fits below `T_S,max`), R* perfect-foresight optimum over 24 h by dynamic programming (state `T_S`, exact up to a 0.25 K grid; not an LP because the duty is non-linear in state and flow). Terminal condition and energy correction: same stored energy as R0 at the end. Grid: discarded heat none / 100 / 300 kW / day profile / 800 kW; volume 5 / 10 / 20 / 30 / 50 m3; weather both days, -5 / 0 / +5 K.

**b) R0 check.** Product 1 reproduced (steam -0.2 %, storage temperature RMSE 1.8 K). Product 2 not by the pre-registered criterion (steam -1.0 %, but storage temperature RMSE 7.8 K, max 11.0 K): one preheater conductance does not describe the day (Befund 91).

**c) Result by the pre-registered rule.** Realistic scenarios (discarded heat > 0, volume <= 20 m3): 72; all reach a saving of at least 5 % of the daily steam energy (17-76 % at the reference scenarios, e.g. product 1, 300 kW, 10 m3: R0 13 763, R1 7 848, R* 7 793 kWh/d, CO2 3 074 / 1 753 / 1 740 kg/d; product 2: 7 359 / 3 116 / 2 770 kWh/d, 1 643 / 696 / 619 kg/d); the gap R1 - R* is at least 2 % in 29 of them, all on product 2. Reading by the letter: **L1** (product 1: L2; product 2: L1; conservative subset `Q_dump <= 300 kW`: L1).

**d) Why this must not be quoted alone.** (i) Decomposition of the saving: exchanger use 0 kWh/d, timing and temperature level 0-1 kWh/d, extra heat used 100 % (saving / extra heat taken = 0.997-0.998 in all 120 scenarios with discarded heat). Without discarded heat R0, R1 and R* agree within 1 kWh/d in every scenario: the duty is flat above about 15 m3/h of preheater-loop flow, the logged flow is already at the peak, a larger flow gives slightly less. (ii) The gap on product 2 is a property of the max-flow rule; post-hoc, the plain rule R1b (logged flow plus all discarded heat) leaves at most 0.9 % (product 1: below 0.1 %) and the gate rule with R1b reads **L2** on both days. (iii) The model lets all heat entering the storage leave over the preheater (storage loss negligible), so the saving equals the added energy up to `T_S,max`; whether the heat exists and the loop can take it is a process-integration question, not a control question.

**e) Sensitivity ranking (change of the R* saving, kWh/d, product 1 / 2).** `T_S,max` 75 / 100 degC: -2112 / -2696 and +858 / +1461; exchanger conductances (other day's fit, x0.8, x1.25): up to +1187 / -2367; topology A: +73 / +167; humidity, `UA_S`, reference volume of the base heat: below 50; maximum flow, `T_S,min`: below 10; fan heat fraction and boiler efficiency change percentages and CO2, not kWh.

**f) Not concluded.** No statement that discarded compressor heat exists, nor how much; no saving figure for the plant; no statement about RL (no RL was built or run). The result says: in this model, what could be gained is energy that has to be added to the storage loop, and a plain rule takes it; memory-dependent decisions add at most 0.9 % of the daily steam energy on the grid. Questions for the partner: discarded compressor heat and whether the loop can absorb it; maximum storage temperature and compressor cooling-water limit; exchanger design data and the air flow through the preheater; loop order; storage volume; boiler efficiency.

**g) Files.** `src/twinlink_ml/storage_a1/scheduling.py`, `tests/test_storage_a1_scheduling.py` (DP against brute force), `scripts/gate_storage_shift.py`, `scripts/analyze_gate_storage_shift.py`, `docs/18_storage_plant_a.md` section 9.

**h) Additions after the review by the project lead (2026-10-15).** (1) **Formal reading: L1 by the rule fixed beforehand** (product 2: L1; product 1: L2; conservative subset `Q_dump <= 300 kW`: L1; the pre-registered rule applied to the policies R0, R1 and R* as defined in a)). (2) **L2 is a post-hoc reading, marked as such:** it was computed after the gate result because R1 ("maximum flow while `T_S > T_S,min`") was a weak rule; with the plain rule R1b (logged flow plus all discarded heat) the gate reads L2 on both days (d, ii). The pre-registered verdict is not replaced by it. (3) **The saving comes entirely from using discarded heat** (a placeholder without a measured source): 100 % of it is extra heat taken (d, i); **pure shifting in time saves about nothing** (timing and temperature level 0-1 kWh/d). The **storage capacity corresponds to about one hour of heating demand** (statement of the project lead, not recomputed here). (4) **Decision (project lead): no S3.**

### 93. Closure of the one-step bandit (follow-up of Befund 68, entry of its own): residual action and separated moisture cost lift SAC from a negative to a clearly positive closed-regret fraction, but no cell meets the feasibility gate -- RL stays a diagnostic finding at this limit

Follow-up of Befund 68 (the Lagrangian treatment, where the multiplier was never active); an entry of its own by decision of the project lead (2026-10-15). **Placeholders (every number below inherits them):** quality limit 0.15 kg/kg (main case), lower gas-velocity bound 0.80 m/s (`ActionBound`, unchanged), critical moisture 0.20 of the kinetics, penalty weight 50 kW and margin m = 0.005961819615175404 kg/kg are settings or earlier choices, not sourced values. Test set (always named): the 25 Befund 52 grid points with oracle and fixed operating point of the limit 0.15 (`s05_limit015_oracle_and_fixed`).

**Question and design.** Up to Befund 68 / SH no agent got past the fixed operating point. Two suspected causes were tested, alone and together (2 x 2, cells `base` = arm C of S0.6 run by the new script, `sep`, `res`, `ressep`): (R) a residual action, executed action = clip(a_fixed + 0.5 * delta), last actor layer zero-initialised so that the policy is exactly the fixed point at step 0; (S) a separated moisture cost: solver failures and solved points with any infeasibility reason other than "moisture above the critical moisture" are masked (not stored, counted), the +1 term (50 kW) for moisture above the critical moisture is removed and only the smooth cost lambda_b * g_tilde remains (my reading of "smooth, normalised cost"; no extra penalty term). Lagrange per context cell as in S0.3 (5 x 5, lambda_0 0.5, eta 0.2 kW, every 250 steps). SAC defaults, seeds 0-4, one run of 30 000 steps with checkpoints; the budget "10 000" is its checkpoint (SAC has no schedule that depends on the planned length). Residual range 0.5 (+-15 K, +-0.425 m/s) fixed beforehand from the S0.5 reference: 24 of 25 oracle points lie within it. Design and gate fixed in `scripts/run_rl_bandit_residual.py` and `scripts/analyze_bres_gate.py` (commit `6dd095d`, before any run). Full suite before the runs: exit code 0, no failure; full suite again after the runs, at the code of `6dd095d` plus documentation and artifacts only: **884 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed** (two known skips, 13 for the partner files in `local/` that exist only in the main checkout; `test_denylist.py` ran with `local/denylist.txt` and passed); all 20 run records `git/dirty=False` (records commit `09a5a64`, 5-6 h wall time per run at 0.6-0.65 s per step on a machine shared with other runs). Artifact `bres_gate.json` (commit `3f57239`).

**Gate (fixed beforehand):** feasibility 1.0 (read strictly: in every seed); median pooled closed fraction > 0 (stage 1) or > 0.5 (stage 2). **Result: not met in any cell, at either budget.** Step 30 000, median over 5 seeds (min to max):

| cell | feasibility | pooled closed fraction | distance to the limit at the binding contexts, units of m | lambda series not inactive (of 125) | masked steps per run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (no R, no S) | 1.00 (0.80-1.00) | -0.639 (-1.519 to -0.177) | 5.38 (4.61-8.15) | 2 | 0 |
| sep (S) | 0.92 (0.60-1.00) | 0.781 (0.689-0.788) | 1.13 (0.27-1.53) | 125 | 19-34 |
| res (R) | 0.64 (0.60-0.84) | 0.645 (0.351-0.894) | 1.02 (0.11-2.28) | 96 | 0 |
| ressep (R and S) | 0.88 (0.60-1.00) | 0.906 (0.824-0.944) | 0.94 (0.24-1.18) | 125 | 0 |

Step 10 000: base 1.00 / -3.121; sep 0.68 / 0.263; res 0.80 / 0.232; ressep feasibility 0.04 (0.00-0.36), the pooled fraction is undefined in two seeds and -269 in a third (the policies sit 2-3 m beyond the true limit at that step and come back by step 20 000). The start value of both residual cells at step 0 is 1.7e-15 in all seeds (fixed point reproduced). One single run meets feasibility 1.0 and stage 2 (ressep, seed 2: 1.00, 0.824); that is not a median.

**Which measure carries the effect** (pre-registered rule, SX1 two-sample thresholds, step 30 000): contrasts of the median pooled fraction R|S0 (res - base) +1.28 (threshold 0.72), R|S1 (ressep - sep) +0.124 (0.070), S|R0 (sep - base) +1.42 (0.73), S|R1 (ressep - res) +0.26 (0.29, not resolved). By the rule: "mixed". Read in words: either measure alone lifts the median from -0.64 to 0.64-0.78; the separated cost (S) is the larger and the more reliable single step (range 0.689-0.788 against 0.351-0.894 for R); R adds a small resolved +0.12 on top of S and moves the agent onto the tightened limit (0.94 m); S added to R is not resolved at five seeds. The multiplier got its signal: 125 of 125 series active with S (base: 2 of 125), all `ressep` series converged by the S0.3 categories.

**What the numbers do and do not say (evidence, not proof).** (a) The critic sees a much easier regression with the two measures: median critic loss of the first 100 logged updates 188-340 (base), 160-304 (sep), 0.15-42 (res), 0.15-0.25 (ressep); of the last 100 updates 0.075-0.51 (base), 0.012-0.022 (sep), 0.003-0.068 (res), 0.001 or below (ressep) (per-seed ranges, from the step traces). That is consistent with the cliff and the failure value having been an obstacle, but it does not separate them from the larger starting error of an untrained absolute policy. (b) The gate fails on feasibility, not on regret: the agents settle at the tightened limit (distance about 1 m) and the true limit 0.15 is exceeded at 0-40 % of the test contexts per seed, because the margin m (0.006 kg/kg) is small against the policy error; the pooled fraction counts feasible points only, and the reachable ceiling of the residual box with the oracle action clipped into it is 0.818 (feasibility 1.0), so values above it (0.906 in `ressep`) come with infeasible points at the binding contexts. (c) Not tested, because the instruction was one closed 2 x 2 and margins are not mine to change: a larger margin or the shield of SH1 at deployment. (d) `base` at step 10 000 against arm C of S0.6 (same seeds and settings, run by a different script, one thread): per-seed pooled differences -2.0 to +1.6, median -3.12 against -1.88; not bit-reproducible, of the order of the resolution threshold 1.6. Caveats: five seeds; one limit; thresholds with `nu_eff` 3.76; the distance is defined at the oracle-binding contexts only.

**Classification.** With a residual start and a separated moisture cost SAC closes about 0.9 of the regret (median, 30 000 steps) at 88 % median feasibility, but it does not reach the direct optimisation (1.0 and feasible everywhere) under the pre-registered gate; RL stays a diagnostic finding and a comparison arm, as at the end of Befund 68. Artifacts: `bres_gate`; records `rl_bandit_residual_{base,sep,res,ressep}_*` (commits `09a5a64`, `3f57239`).

**Citation rule (added after the review by the project lead, 2026-10-15).** The median pooled closed fraction **0.906 of the cell `ressep` lies above the reachable admissible ceiling 0.818 of the residual box** (the oracle action clipped into the box, feasibility 1.0; b above). A value above the ceiling cannot be reached by feasible points alone: it is carried by points that violate the true limit (infeasible at the binding contexts) and is **not to be quoted as a performance figure**; the same holds for the "about 0.9 of the regret" of the classification above. What can be quoted: feasibility 0.88 (0.60-1.00) and the distance of 0.94 m (units of m) to the tightened limit of the same cell, and that the gate is not met in any cell.

### Befund 95 (2026-10-15): flowsheet of the partner model from exchangeable units -- one switch per assumption, decomposition, ranking of the scenarios

Branch `partner-units` (not merged, not pushed). Full text and tables: `docs/11_partner_model_v4.md`, section 11, written so that it can go to the partner as feedback. Code `src/twinlink_ml/flowsheet/` (units `DryerBlock`, `HeatExchanger`, `HeatTransferLoop`, `Preheater`, `Burner`, class `Flowsheet`), tests `tests/test_flowsheet_units.py` (units, Befund-90 artifact, mirror pairs, walks) and `tests/test_flowsheet_workbook.py` (needs `local/`, skipped without it), script `scripts/report_partner_flowsheet.py` (commit `7f6b8b8`), artifact `artifacts/runs/partner_flowsheet_decomposition.json` (`git/dirty=False`). Model against model, no plant data.

**What was built.** The units of the partner model existed twice (rebuild of Befund 74, physical alternatives of Befunde 75-90). They are now behind one interface; seven switches, each `partner` | `physical`: exchanger (equal outlet temperatures | counter-current with `dT_min` along the exchanger; main convention per exchanger, sensitivity through the circuit as in Befund 90), `cp_gas` (1.2 | 1.006 and the vapour property of the repository), condensation, heat loss (`UA` 2 W/K, laboratory placeholder), product moisture (equilibrium 2 g/kg | laboratory model, dryer 2 only, an extrapolation), gas formula (as built | corrected), boiling check (flag only). Fan and pump power are outputs (placeholders without source) and enter the CO2 with the factors of `carrier_energy`. The numerics of the physical side were lifted unchanged from `scripts/report_heat_recovery_comparison.py`, which now imports them. Separately committed before: the helper `sanjay_inputs` of `scripts/report_dryer_block_vs_bed.py` (named after a person) was renamed `partner_inputs` (and `_block_for_sanjay` `_block_for_partner`), no other caller existed.

**Reproduction.** All switches `partner` against every stored number of the sheet `Scenarios`: 230 cells, largest relative difference 2.0e-15 (tolerance of the workbook tests 1e-12). With the gas formula corrected only rows 26, 39, 41 differ, by 108.911. Switches `physical` / `partner` against Befund 90 with its source-variant exhausts pinned: 156 scenario rows, largest difference 0.0 kW and 4.4e-16 kg/h. The Befund-90 script on the lifted units (`heat_recovery_comparison_r3_units.json`, commit `8c587b4`) equals `heat_recovery_comparison_r2.json` in all 113 524 numbers. Mirror pairs 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 have equal fuel, recovery and CO2 in every state.

**Decomposition** (two orders of the switches, two conventions of `dT_min`, `dT_min` 10 K; 4 x 8 steps; each switch alone in both directions). **The ranking of the scenarios, 1 = 2 < 5 = 6 < 3 = 4 (CO2 of the corrected fuel plus placeholder electricity, lowest first; identical by fuel and by recovered heat), holds in every step**; smallest gap between neighbouring groups 0.022 kg CO2/h. Partner model to all-`physical` (scenarios 1 / 3 / 5): recovery 1.777 / 1.420 / 1.606 to 2.205 / 1.709 / 1.795 kW, corrected fuel 1.2363 / 1.2720 / 1.2534 to 0.9662 / 1.0158 / 1.0071 kg/h. For the fuel `cp_gas` is the largest single switch (-0.17 to -0.18 kg/h), the exchanger the second (-0.09 to -0.14 kg/h); condensation 0 at 10 K per exchanger, 0.36 kW in scenario 1 at 10 K through the circuit; the effects depend on the order (exchanger +1.42 kW in scenario 1 from the partner model, -0.99 kW from the all-`physical` state). Boiling flag: one stage per scenario in the partner model, none with the physical exchanger at 10 K per exchanger. Electricity is 0.43 kW in each scenario (placeholders) and cannot reorder them by construction.

**Findings that qualify earlier results (reported, nothing changed; to be confirmed by the project lead).** (1) Befund 90 columns b-d use repository gas properties in the exchangers but dryer exhausts computed with the partner's `cp_gas` 1.2 (72.28 / 134.66 degC); with one property set for the whole flowsheet the exhausts are 58.94 / 108.93 degC (56.26 / 108.25 with heat loss and product moisture), and the all-`physical` recovery of scenario 1 is 2.672 kW against 3.662 kW in column c (10 K through the circuit). Ranking and mechanism of Befund 90 are unaffected, its absolute figures belong to a mixed property set. (2) The block of the equation document gives 108.25 degC for dryer 2 in the all-`physical` state against 103.49 degC of the laboratory model; the remaining 4.8 K come from constants that are not switches (not examined). With dryer 2 pinned to the bed state the recovery is 2.094 / 1.598 / 1.684 kW instead of 2.205 / 1.709 / 1.795 kW, same ranking.

**Caveats.** Placeholders: `dT_min` and its convention, `UA`, dew-point margin, `T_kalt`, fan and pump numbers. Product moisture `physical` for dryer 2 only (an extrapolation of the laboratory model). Decision taken without asking (unattended): `Preheater` is the pre-heating train of one sink; the `cp_gas` switch exchanges gas and vapour properties together (as the step of Befund 90 does); the heat loss acts on the dryers only; the ranking metric is CO2.

Dryer 2, the remaining 4.8 K (documented only, not examined; Befund 95).** In the all-`physical` flowsheet the dryer block gives 108.25 degC for dryer 2 against 103.49 degC of the laboratory model. Constants that differ between the block and the bed model and are not switches (from `docs/11`, section 9.2): heat capacity of the suspension (bed: fixed 3500 J/(kg K); block: mixture rule, 2920 at solid fraction 0.4), slope of the evaporation enthalpy (bed: -2358.6 J/(kg K), consistent with a vapour heat capacity of 1821 instead of its own 1860; block: `cp_v - cp_l`), heat capacities of liquid and solid (bed 4180 / 1200; block 4200 / 1000) and the evaporation enthalpy at 0 degC (bed 2500.8 kJ/kg; block 2500). Which of them accounts for how much of the 4.8 K is not known.

**9. Assumptions of Befund 95 (listed as requested; confirmed by the project lead on 2026-10-15).** (1) The ranking of the scenarios is by CO2 of the corrected fuel plus the placeholder electricity, lowest first; the rankings by fuel and by recovered heat are identical in every step. (2) The main convention of `dT_min` is 10 K per exchanger; 10 K through the circuit (5 K per exchanger) is the sensitivity of Befund 90. (3) `UA` 2 W/K is the laboratory placeholder, applies to the dryers only, and is not a plant value. (4) `Preheater` is the pre-heating train of one sink (its stages in the drawn order). (5) The `cp_gas` switch exchanges the gas and the vapour property together (as the step of Befund 90 does). (6) Product moisture `physical` applies to dryer 2 only and is an extrapolation of the laboratory model; dryer 1 keeps the equilibrium moisture. (7) Fan and pump power are outputs with placeholders without a source (pressure drops 4 kPa per dryer line, 0.5 kPa per exchanger side, 1 bar per circuit; the efficiencies of the laboratory process); they cannot reorder the scenarios by construction. (8) The boiling check is a flag at 100 degC (1 atm) and never caps a temperature.

### Befund 96 (2026-10-15): margin needed by the RL policy (cell `ressep` of Befund 93) -- k = 5 meets the feasibility gate at 6.9 % extra energy over the optimiser with margin m; addendum to Befund 93

Addendum to Befund 93 (no existing finding changed). *Numbering:* this entry was prepared as "Befund 95" (working label in the docstrings of `scripts/analyze_bres_margin.py`, `scripts/run_bres_margin_references.py`, `scripts/run_rl_bandit_residual.py` and in the study artifacts); master assigned Befund 95 to the flowsheet entry meanwhile, so it is entered as Befund 96. **Placeholders (every number inherits them):** quality limit 0.15 kg/kg (main case), lower gas-velocity bound 0.80 m/s (`ActionBound`, unchanged), critical moisture 0.20 of the kinetics, penalty weight 50 kW and the margin m = 0.005961819615175404 kg/kg are settings or earlier choices, not sourced values. Test set (always named): the 25 Befund 52 grid points; references of the closed fraction as in Befund 93 (`s05_limit015_oracle_and_fixed`).

**Question.** Which margin `k * m` does the policy of the cell `ressep` need to be feasible against the TRUE limit 0.15 in every seed, and what does it cost against the optimiser? **Design (fixed beforehand in the docstring of `scripts/analyze_bres_margin.py`, commit `472b871`, before any run).** Only `ressep`, otherwise as Befund 93 (residual radius 0.5, separated cost, Lagrange per context cell); margin `k * m` with k in {2, 3, 5} (k = 1 from the records of Befund 93), seeds 0-4, 30 000 steps, torch threads fixed to 1 (`--margin-factor`, default 1.0 reproduces the old runs). References with the same margin `k * m` and with m as common reference: oracle (k = 1, 2, 3, 5) and fixed operating point (k = 2, 3, 5), legacy objective `energy_target`, Befund 52 budget, existing optimisers (`scripts/run_bres_margin_references.py`; artifacts `bres_margin_ref_{oracle,fixed}_k*`, all `git/dirty=False` at commit `472b871`, committed as `886878c`; all 25 oracle contexts feasible, fixed points feasible everywhere). Runs: 15 records `rl_bandit_residual_b_k{2,3,5}_ressep_*`, `git/dirty=False` at `886878c`, committed as `a7a38e3`. Evaluation: artifact `bres_margin` (`git/dirty=False`, commit `a7a38e3`); the 30 000-step checkpoints are re-evaluated and cross-checked against the run records (feasibility and pooled fraction identical in all 20 runs, including the k = 1 runs of Befund 93).

**Gate (fixed beforehand):** smallest k with feasibility 1.0 in every seed at step 30 000. **Result: k = 5.** Feasibility per seed: k = 1: 0.80 / 0.60 / 1.00 / 0.88 / 0.96; k = 2: 1.00 / 0.84 / 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00; k = 3: 1.00 / 0.96 / 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00; k = 5: 1.00 in all five seeds. Table, median over 5 seeds (min to max):

| k | closed A (feasible contexts only) | closed B (infeasible counts 0) | B / ceiling 0.818 | distance to true limit, units of m | extra energy over Oracle(m), % | margin part, % | policy part, % | extra CO2 over Oracle(m), % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (Befund 93) | 0.906 (0.824-0.944), above ceiling in 5 of 5 | 0.819 (0.583-0.895) | 1.00 (0.71-1.09) | 0.94 (0.24-1.18) | 0.66 (-0.07-1.54) | 0 | 0.66 | 0.38 (-0.36-1.16) |
| 2 | 0.760 (0.597-0.870), above ceiling in 1 of 5 | 0.702 (0.597-0.870) | 0.86 (0.73-1.06) | 1.81 (1.10-2.65) | 2.06 (1.14-3.41) | 1.53 | 0.53 | 1.67 (0.79-2.99) |
| 3 | 0.602 (0.475-0.644) | 0.602 (0.475-0.644) | 0.74 (0.58-0.79) | 2.71 (2.33-3.05) | 3.19 (3.02-4.41) | 3.11 | 0.05 | 2.80 (2.61-3.97) |
| 5 | 0.172 (0.023-0.250) | 0.172 (0.023-0.250) | 0.21 (0.03-0.31) | 4.88 (4.53-5.40) | 6.91 (6.27-8.15) | 6.53 | 0.38 (-0.26-1.61) | 6.41 (5.78-7.61) |

Margin part = Oracle(k m) - Oracle(m), policy part = RL(k m) - Oracle(k m), both in per cent of Oracle(m) on the context set S of each seed (contexts at which the policy is feasible and both oracles are; S is the full grid in every seed of k = 5, in 21-25 contexts for k = 2 and 24-25 for k = 3; the k = 1 rows cover 15-25 contexts and are therefore not comparable with the others). The fixed operating point with the margin k m costs 10.5 % (k = 2), 11.7 % (k = 3) and 14.3 % (k = 5) over Oracle(m) on the same energy measure, i.e. more than the policy at the same margin (2.1 / 3.2 / 6.9 %).

**Reading (one sentence, as pre-agreed).** RL needs 5*m margin, additional cost 6.9 % energy (6.4 % CO2) over the optimiser with m (median over 5 seeds, range 6.3-8.1 %); of that 6.5 points are the margin itself (the optimiser pays it too) and 0.4 points (range -0.3 to 1.6) the policy.

**What the numbers do and do not say.** (a) The gate is met at k = 5 only by the pre-registered strict reading, and at the 25 grid contexts only; k = 3 misses it by one context in one seed (24 of 25, seed 1), k = 2 by four contexts in one seed (seed 1: 0.84). The distance to the true limit grows roughly in proportion to the margin (0.94, 1.81, 2.71, 4.88 m), i.e. the agents sit near the tightened limit at every k; (b) The closed fraction falls with k by construction, because `E_fixed` and `E_oracle` of the test set are those of the margin-free limit 0.15; it is a measure of how much of the margin-free regret is left, not a performance loss of the policy (the policy part is small at every k). The fraction of variant A exceeds the reachable admissible ceiling 0.818 in all five seeds of k = 1 and in one seed of k = 2; by the citation rule of Befund 93 those values are carried by infeasible contexts and are not performance figures (the table shows them with that flag only, and k = 3, 5 are below the ceiling). The ceiling with the margin of the reference (oracle of `0.15 - k m` clipped into the box) is stored in the artifact; its fraction is small or negative (0.16, 0.08, 0.02, -0.20 for k = 1, 2, 3, 5) because the margin cost exceeds the margin-free regret of the test set (fixed - oracle). (c) The cost over Oracle(m) is on the feasible contexts of a seed; at k = 1-3 these sets differ between seeds and the policy part may be negative (the policy may sit closer to the true limit than the tightened limit of the oracle). It carries no rank claim; the seed range is the reading. (d) Not tested, as agreed: the shield of SH1, margins between the tested values (k = 4 would lie between the failing k = 3 and the passing k = 5), a margin that depends on the context. (e) References from the current solver (Befund 79 K1) against test-set references of Befund 93 from the older one: differences of the order 1e-5 kW (anchor `m1_anchor_s05_k1`, Befund 80). The oracle chooses the nozzle pressure freely, the RL environment fixes it (as in Befund 93). Caveats: five seeds, one limit, 25 contexts, descriptive.

**Tests.** Full suite at commit `13eadb6` (code of `472b871` plus run records and artifacts): 961 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed (counted from the progress dots; the `-q` configuration prints no summary line; the 15 skips are the same number as in Befund 93); new tests `tests/test_bres_margin_analysis.py` (6). `test_denylist.py` ran with `local/denylist.txt` and passed; ruff clean.

**Procedure note.** The first start of the 15 runs was killed by a restart of the machine at 10 000-20 000 steps (SAC state, replay buffer and optimiser state are not saved, so a continuation is not possible); the partial records were moved out of the repository unchanged and all 15 runs were started afresh with the same commit, settings and prefixes; the finished oracle references of that start (k = 1, 2) were kept. A second start attempt stopped at once at the clean-tree check (reference artifacts uncommitted, no run executed); after committing the references the 15 runs ran through. The re-run values of k = 2, seed 0 at 2 500 and 10 000 steps equal those of the aborted start (checked on that run only). Artifacts: `bres_margin`, `bres_margin_ref_*`; records `rl_bandit_residual_b_k*_ressep_*` (commits `472b871`, `886878c`, `a7a38e3`, analysis artifact `13eadb6`).


### Befund 97 (2026-10-16): joint timing measurement on an idle machine -- inference cost of the methods of study A (incl. the simulator channel of the hybrid) and of the eight architectures of the re-run

**What was measured.** Script `scripts/measure_joint_timing.py` (commit `6b77a16`, committed before the run; artifacts `joint_timing_idle` and `a1_inference_time_v2_idle`, both from a clean tree; the run itself was started by an unattended session after the merges of Befunde 94-96, nothing else was started on the machine). Machine: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X (8 cores, 16 logical CPUs), one thread (`OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS` = 1, `torch.set_num_threads(1)`), warm-up excluded, 300 repeats for the batch of one window (latency), 15 for the whole test set (throughput). Idle criterion fixed in the script: machine load <= 5 % and no other Python process above 5 % of one core; met at the start (load 0 %), between the parts (3 %) and at the end (1 %); no other Python process in any check. This is the first measurement of study A on an idle machine (the two earlier ones, `a1_inference_time_1thread` and `a1_inference_time_v2_background`, ran beside foreign processes; Befund 88 f). Part A: study A, plant P0, seed 1, 64 runs, as in the earlier measurement. Part B: the eight architectures of the re-run on the pool of arm N (preset version 2), seed 1, `n_train` 64, excited test set (4352 windows, as in part A); the networks were fitted for 2 epochs only (the weights do not change the cost of `predict`; their accuracy is not used).

**Part A: study A, microseconds (median), batch of one window / per window in the batch.**

| method | latency, batch 1 | per window, batched |
|---|---|---|
| persistence | 3 | 0.2 |
| ARX | 248 | 4.0 |
| simulator only | 7 | 0.7 |
| from scratch (LSTM) | 2966 | 16.7 |
| hybrid, network part | 2987 | 16.9 |
| pretrain + fine-tune (LSTM) | 2967 | 17.7 |

**The hybrid needs the simulator ahead of the prediction.** One horizon (36 steps of 25 s) of the open simulation for one window: 253 136 us (median; minimum 167 218), i.e. **98.8 % of the hybrid's total real-time cost of 256 123 us** (network 2987 us). Batched over all 4352 test windows the simulator channel costs 250.8 us per window against 16.9 us for the network (hybrid total 267.7 us per window). If the channel is computed ahead for the planned inputs of a whole run (7.33 s per 8 h run, 1152 steps), the cost is 6361 us per prediction at one prediction per sample, total 9349 us. One simulator step costs 7103 us; the steady-state solve at the start of a run 0.16 s. The network alone (2987 us) is not the cost of the hybrid. The earlier non-idle figures (hybrid total 231 860 us, from scratch 2220 us, pretrain + fine-tune 3498 us) lie within the spread of foreign load.

**Part B: the eight architectures (arm N pool, `n_train` 64), microseconds.**

| method | parameters | latency, batch 1 | per window, batched | fit, s per epoch (2-epoch fit, indicative) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| persistence | - | 3 | 0.2 | - |
| static regression | 45 | 5 | 1.7 | - |
| ARX | 102 | 246 | 3.9 | - |
| GRU | 42 819 | 4753 | 123.7 | 4.3 |
| LSTM | 57 027 | 6502 | 57.2 | 4.7 |
| Transformer | 23 523 | 31 567 | 2691.8 | 67.6 |
| xLSTM | 8649 | 27 487 | 936.8 | 27.8 |
| Mamba | 8139 | 14 950 | 415.8 | 14.8 |

Reading: per prediction every learned architecture is far below the sample time of 25 s; the batched cost per window orders LSTM < GRU < Mamba < xLSTM < Transformer, the latency of one window GRU < LSTM < Mamba < xLSTM < Transformer. **The LSTM is faster than the GRU per window in the batch although it has 33 % more parameters (57 027 against 42 819), and the GRU is faster at batch 1 (4753 against 6502 us)**; the observation "LSTM faster than GRU" (Befund 63a, a different machine and model set, not compared here) is therefore, on this machine, a statement about the batch, not about the latency of one window. The fit times per epoch come from a 2-epoch fit and include setup; they are an indication of the training cost, not the cost of a training to convergence, and not comparable with the records of the re-run (parallel load).

**Caveats.** One run of the whole measurement (no repetition across sessions); the medians of 300 (batch 1) and 15 (batch) repeats carry the spread of one process. The machine-load probe of single models shows isolated readings above the idle limit after the measurement of the simulator-only model (74 % after, 12 % before; a 5 s probe of the machine, not of the process; a model of 7 us, not affecting any statement here). Weights untrained to convergence; the inference cost does not depend on them. Placeholders: none of the numbers is a statement about the plant. Part B times only `predict` (no data windowing, no evaluation).

### Befund 99 (2026-10-16): storage test 1, time-slice pinch -- upper bound for the benefit of an ideal heat storage; gate reading L2 (a rule suffices), potential only through an assumed compressor load profile

Branch `storage-timeslice`, merged into `master` on 2026-10-16. *Numbering:* prepared as "Befund 98"; master assigned 98 to the Holm addendum to Befund 94 meanwhile, so this entry is Befund 99; the scripts, artifacts and `docs/19` of the branch keep the working label "Befund 98" where they carry one. Full text, tables, questions for the partner: `docs/19_storage_time_slice.md`. **Scenario band on placeholders, not a plant statement; every number carries its scenario.** No RL.

**Question.** How much fossil residual heat can an IDEAL storage save at most, compared with using heat only when it occurs (problem table per 15-minute step), and does a rule without foresight reach it? Gate fixed beforehand in the docstring of `scripts/gate_storage_timeslice.py` (commit `ee159d9`, before any computation): L1 (RL/MPC justified) = a cell with saving >= 5 % of the daily fossil residual heat AND rule gap >= 2 points; L2 = saving >= 5 % but rule within 2 points; L3 = saving < 5 % everywhere; cells = scenario x capacity <= 10 MWh, all placeholders inside their bands.

**Method (new package `twinlink_ml.storage_timeslice`, tests `tests/test_storage_timeslice*.py`).** Direct hot utility from the problem table (`heatnetwork.pinch` segments and condensation sampling reused); the ideal storage at one level `T_S` (30-80 degC) enters the table as an isothermal cold (charging) and hot (discharging) stream with approach `dT_min` on each side, which makes the step utility a maximum of 3 linear pieces and the whole horizon one LP (cyclic, no power limits, loss 0 and 0.5 %/h); rule = discharge as much as lowers the utility, charge the surplus that does not raise it, cyclic. Checks: C = 0 gives E_direct; balance closed (1.1e-10 kWh); E_ideal non-increasing; E_rule >= E_ideal; LP utility equals the problem table with the isothermal streams added explicitly; toy case solved by hand. A first version treated the discharging boundary inclusively and overstated the saving; the comparison test against the explicit-stream table caught it before any run.

**Scenarios.** Sources: compressor heat plant A 400/800/1200 kW (85 -> 45 degC), plant C 2.4 GWh/a, exhaust of plant A (both measured days; humidity reconstructed from the spray rate, solid fraction 0.3, saturation cap), exhaust of plant C (2 lines of 20 000 Nm3/h); sinks: process air A (measured; mean 957 / 798 kW without fan credit, 852 / 697 kW with it as in Befund 91), process air C, hall heating 0/200 kW, process water 0/200 kW; modes flat / shift / weekly; weather -10/-5/0/+5 K; C = 0 ... 20 MWh. Main grid 2240 scenarios plus 68 reference and sensitivity runs. Artifact `gate_storage_timeslice` (script commit `db8a646`, clean tree, `git/dirty=False`, committed as `f8ec7e6`).

**Result.** **L2.** 11 540 cells, 1420 with saving >= 5 %, none with a rule gap (largest 3.9e-15). Main grid: 339 of 2240 scenarios (15.1 %) have a cell >= 5 %, **all on the product-2 day** (product 1: maximum 2.6 %); mode flat: maximum 3.0 % (L3 for that mode); conditions closest to the measured days (plant A, flat, no hall, no process water): 0.0 % (L3). Largest saving fraction 20.2 % (plant A, product 2, day, shift, -10 K, compressor 1200 kW, hall 200, water 0, 2 MWh: 1459 of 7211 kWh/d), largest absolute 1696 kWh/d (A+C, product 2, week, shift, -10 K, compressor 800 kW, hall 0, water 0: 15.7 %). The saving saturates at about 2 MWh (one cycle per day; 90 % at 2 MWh); day and week agree in mode shift; losses cost little (the surplus is free).

**Decomposition (5 MWh).** The saving sits in compressor heat -> process air; in the full network of the two pre-registered references (A+C, product 1) it is 0: the process air of plant A absorbs the compressor heat directly, network integration replaces the storage. A multi-level (stratified) ideal storage adds nothing in three scenarios and 162 kWh/d (1.5 % of E_direct) in the largest-kWh one. **Sensitivity.** The pre-registered references have a saving of 0, so variants can only open it (storage approach `dT_min/2`: +781 kWh/d, the only product-1 cell above 5 %; exhaust C by annual figure, compressor temperatures 90-50, `dT_min` 10 K). Two further references with a non-zero saving were fixed after seeing this (declared post-hoc; script `scripts/analyze_storage_timeslice_sensitivity.py` committed before its run; artifact `gate_storage_timeslice_posthoc_sensitivity`, clean tree): ranking by effect: compressor level and process-air demand (product day), compressor load contrast and shift window, `dT_min`, compressor temperatures, plant-C items, weather; not by exhaust humidity, `T_kalt` or loss rate. Questions for the partner in `docs/19`, section 8 (compressor heat time series first).

**Caveats.** (1) The letter L2 is the best case over the bands and must not be quoted alone; the driver, the compressor load profile, is a placeholder; with constant operation there is nothing to shift. (2) Two measured days; product 2 carries every above-5 % cell. (3) Ideal storage (no power limit, perfect exchangers); a greedy rule equals the programme by structure, so L1 cannot occur in this model (a gap would need power limits, several storages, source forecasts) -- this says nothing about other limits. (4) The exhaust of plant C by volume flow is 4.9 times the partner's annual figure (999 against 205 kW mean). (5) 139 rule results (day horizon, C >= 2 MWh) did not reach the periodic steady state in 60 cycles; their gap is below 1.1e-15 anyway. (6) Placeholders throughout: compressor levels and temperatures, load profiles, hall and process-water demand, plant-C flows and annual figures, solid fraction, humidity, `dT_min`, `T_kalt`, loss rate; none of the numbers is a statement about the plant.


### Addendum (2026-10-19) to Befund 99: re-check with an energy-balance-admissible solid fraction (0.60 / 0.634 / 0.70); the readings stand, two sensitivity numbers move

Addendum to Befund 99 (no number of the entry is changed; `docs/19_storage_time_slice.md` stays as it is, the report of the re-check is `docs/19a_storage_time_slice_solid_fraction_recheck.md`). Branch `storage-timeslice-solid-fraction`. Reason: Befund 99 reconstructs the exhaust humidity of plant A with the solid fraction 0.3 (placeholder, band 0.2-0.5); the operating-point study of plant A (`docs/23`) finds that value inadmissible by the dryer energy balance of the same two days. Script `scripts/recheck_storage_timeslice_solid_fraction.py` (commit `ec64e0f`, committed before any run; it repeats the pre-registered computation of `scripts/gate_storage_timeslice.py` and the post-hoc references R3/R4 with the same grid, capacities, levels and gate definitions; solid fraction set in every scenario; the variants `solid_fraction` 0.2/0.5 dropped, so the gate has 11 520 cells instead of 11 540); artifacts `recheck_storage_timeslice_solid_fraction_{060,0634,070}` (clean tree, `git/dirty=False`, commits `629c6b1`, `7c08870`, `5f89d72`); reader `scripts/report_storage_timeslice_solid_fraction.py`. Control: 116 runs of Befund 99 re-run at 0.3 reproduce `E_direct` and `E_ideal` of its artifacts exactly (difference 0.0 kWh/d). The value 0.634 is the one consistent with both measured days; the product-specific minima of the energy balance are kept locally (confidential values), the band is 0.60-0.70. Placeholders as in Befund 99.

**(i) The conclusions of Befund 99 hold at 0.60, 0.634 and 0.70.** Gate reading L2 in all three runs; 1420 cells with a saving >= 5 %, none with a rule gap >= 2 points; the largest rule gap 3.9e-15; 339 of 2240 main-grid scenarios (15.1 %) with a cell >= 5 %, all on the product-2 day; the groupings and maxima of the gate (site, horizon, day, mode), the table of the main scenarios, the multi-level check (162 kWh/d in the largest-kWh scenario, otherwise 0) and the loss effect are unchanged. The potential still comes from the compressor load profile against the process-air demand; the solid fraction is not needed for that statement. What moves is the exhaust state itself (exhaust heat of plant A down 24-41 %, mostly latent heat below the dew point), the main-grid maximum on the product-1 day (2.59 % at 0.3 against 2.66 / 2.67 / 2.69 %, always far below the 5 % threshold), and `E_direct` of 242 / 244 / 254 product-1 scenarios (largest change of the saving 14 / 41 / 81 kWh/d, 0.10 / 0.31 / 0.60 points); no product-2 scenario changes.

**(ii) A caveat of Befund 99 no longer applies.** "The exhaust of product 2 is capped at saturation in every step" (capped share 1.00 at 0.3) holds only for the placeholder 0.3; with an admissible solid fraction the capped share is 0.00 on both days (reconstructed day-mean outlet humidity of product 2: 0.0353 kg/kg at 0.3 against 0.0273 / 0.0255 / 0.0221 kg/kg).

**(iii) The two sensitivity numbers that move (saving at C = 5 MWh, kWh/d, 0.3 -> 0.60 / 0.634 / 0.70).** R1 "exhaust C by annual figure": +398 -> +175 / +139 / +84 (percentage points +3.6 -> +1.6 / +1.3 / +0.8); its rank in the R1 ranking falls from 2 to 4 (0.60, 0.634) or 6 (0.70). R3 `dT_min` 10 K: +247 -> +114 / +88 / +51 (+3.2 -> +1.5 / +1.2 / +0.7 points). Further, smaller moves: the decomposition R1 "leave out exhaust of A opens" 277 -> 263 / 261 / 258 and its largest exhaust pair 28 -> 21 / 20 / 18; R3 "exhaust C by annual figure" 0 -> -29 in all three. R1 `dT_min` 10 K (+249 -> +249 / +250 / +254) and the R2 variants are practically unchanged; `dT_min/2` (+781) and compressor 90-50 (+385) unchanged; the base savings of R3/R4 unchanged. No reading changes; the question to the partner on the exhaust of plant C (volume flow and annual figure read together) keeps its place.

**(iv) Text against artifact in Befund 99 (not caused by the re-check; no reading changes).** `docs/19` section 6 lists the R1 sensitivity as `dT_min/2` +781, annual figure +398, compressor 90-50 +385, `dT_min` 10 K +249 and "everything else 0". The artifact `gate_storage_timeslice` (`sensitivity.R1.ranking`) has four further entries different from 0: low solid fraction 0.1 +114 (+1.0 points), weather -10 K +97 (+0.9), product day 2 +29 (+0.2), hall temperatures 40-30 +19 (+0.2). `docs/19` is not changed (the artifact is the source); this addendum is the correction.

**Caveats.** The band of the solid fraction in `storage_timeslice.config.PLACEHOLDER_BANDS` (0.2-0.5) is unchanged (no unilateral change of a band); with the default config the Befund 99 artifacts reproduce only if 0.3 is passed explicitly. The recheck repeats the scenario band of Befund 99 with one placeholder replaced by a value taken from the operating-point study; it is a scenario band, not a plant statement.
