### Befund 100 (2026-10-16): site pinch -- largest usable waste heat, pinch at the inlet of the warmest waste-heat stream, network at 70-75 / 40-45 degC; the solid fraction of Befund 99 does not move the site result

Branch `site-pinch`, merged into `master` on 2026-10-19 (entered as Befund 100). Full text, tables, figures, questions for the partner: `docs/20_site_pinch.md`. **Scenario grid on placeholders, not a plant statement; every number carries its scenario.** No RL.

**Question.** How much waste heat can the site use at most (minimum fossil heat against today), where is the pinch, which sources and sinks belong together, and at which temperature should the planned waste-heat network run? Exploration fixed in the docstring of `scripts/run_site_pinch.py` before any computation; no gate.

**Method (new package `twinlink_ml.site`, data set `conf/site/site_placeholder.yaml`, tests `tests/test_site.py`).** 12 representative days (the measured days of plant A shifted to the monthly means of a placeholder climate), 96 steps of 15 min, problem table per step on exact ramp sums (no storage; `heatnetwork.pinch` condensation sampling and the `storage_timeslice` streams of Befund 99 reused). Target = minimum hot utility of all site streams; today = recovery inside today's groups (compressor -> plant A capped at 400 kW, plant C's own planned recovery plus 200 kW to hall/process water); saving = fossil today - target. Network level: one loop at (supply, return), `dT_min/2` per exchanger, direct recovery inside each plant, plants on parallel branches, return cooler allowed (zonal LP per step, 13 levels). Heat-pump limits from the grand composite curve (handover to study 2). Grid: plant A day x plant C {volume, annual figure, none} x compressor heat {400, 800, 1200 kW} x further lines {0; 1-5 x 10 000 / 20 000 / 30 000 Nm3/h x product day} x `dT_min` {10, 20 K} x hall/process water {0, 200/200 kW} = 2232 scenarios, six references, one-at-a-time sensitivity around R1 and R5. Artifact `run_site_pinch_sf0634` (script commit `ed0f277`, clean tree, `git/dirty=False`). Checks: energy balance per step (largest residual 4.0e-8 kW); today >= target <= every network level in every run; Befund 99's `direct_kwh_per_day` reproduced for all 896 day-horizon scenarios (3.1e-11); Befund 60 reproduced in the tests (4048.99 kW); single line = heat-network pinch; loop capacity checked along the exchanger with `heatnetwork.approach.max_duty_along`.

**Result.** R1 (plant A product 1, plant C by volume flow, compressor 800 kW, hall/water 200/200 kW, `dT_min` 20 K, no further lines): target 655 kW against 1092 kW fossil today, **saving 436 kW = 3821 MWh/a = 853 t CO2/a** (7.4 % of the site's 11 500 t/a); recovered heat 1573 kW at the target against 1137 kW today. Grid: saving 62-3564 kW (median 993 kW); `dT_min` 10 instead of 20 K adds 100-783 kW. Without further sinks the compressor heat saturates: 800 and 1200 kW give the same target on product 1 (the 80 degC water cannot serve the process air above about 60 degC); the roadmap step from 400 kW to 1.2 MW (+800 kW) exceeds R1's whole remaining potential and is reached (saving > 800 kW) in 1456 of 2232 scenarios, 1452 of them with further lines. The plant C contradiction moves the baseline (plant C's own recovery 737 / 407 kW), the target only by 33 kW (R1 / R3). The partner's 30 GWh/a gas allows at most three to four further lines of 20 000 Nm3/h (four: 28.4 GWh/a, derived). **Pinch:** at the inlet of the warmest waste-heat stream: exhaust of plant A (about 61 / 34 degC) in 1269 scenarios, further lines 439, compressor water (80 degC) 400; below it everything is surplus, above it only the top of the process-air heating (R1: 655 kW above 60 degC on the cold side). **Pairing:** compressor water -> preheating of all process air up to about 60 degC; exhaust -> first preheating stage and process water. **Network level:** 70/40 degC reaches a median 0.97 of the target saving (min 0.79); the best level with supply 70-90 degC reaches >= 0.9 in 96 % of the scenarios, with supply <= 60 degC in 53 %, and the low level is never better by more than 5 points; a low level is best only where the pinch lies below 40 degC (all 806 such scenarios). **Heat pump (handover):** R1 about 345 kW of surplus at >= 30 degC, condenser needed at 85-100 degC (best pair 30 -> 100 degC, COP 2.67, 515 kW, 388 t CO2/a at 0.366 kg/kWh, 669 t/a at 0.20); on the product-2 day the surplus lies below 15 degC.

**Solid fraction (hint of study 4).** Main value 0.634 (band 0.60-0.70; energy balance of plant A, parallel study 4, `docs/23` section 5); the 0.3 of Befund 99 is inadmissible and kept as a paired variant (198 scenarios + R1-R6, artifact `run_site_pinch_sf0634_variant_befund99`, script `1e2770c`, clean tree): it adds 221-1535 kW of (latent) exhaust heat, but changes the saving by only -15 ... +36 kW (median +4 kW), because the extra heat lies below the pinch. A first start with 0.3 as the main value was stopped after 100 of 2340 runs (no artifact). The field `variant_befund_99` of `run_site_pinch_sf0634` is invalid (string "0.3", a shadowed loop variable in the script); fixed in `1e2770c`, the variant is in its own artifact.

**Sensitivity (largest change of the saving, MWh/a, R1 / R5):** further lines 4544 / 5916; their recovery today -- / 3944; plant C reading 2599 / 2418; compressor water supply temperature 2424 / 1829; compressor heat 1659 / 2258; `dT_min` 1119 / 2892; flow of the further lines 0 / 1972; plant C compressor heat 1016 / 417; process water 907 / 154; today's compressor use 876 / 876; climate 430 / 737; `T_kalt`, intake humidity, solid fraction within its band, heater efficiency <= 79. Questions for the partner in `docs/20`, section 10 (further lines first).

**Caveats.** (1) Placeholders throughout; R1 is one cell of the grid. (2) Two measured days; months shift the intake temperature only; further lines are copies of plant A. (3) Target = lower bound (ideal exchangers, no storage); the network model ignores distances, pressure drops and part load. (4) Today's baseline models plant C's planned recovery and 400 kW of compressor use. (5) The exhaust of plant C copies plant A's state; the boiler flue gas uses the specific heats of air.
### Befund 101 (2026-10-16): heat pump on low-temperature waste heat -- pays in every scenario of the grid, by CO2 and by cost, as a booster across the pinch on top of direct recovery; Stage-B gate reading L1, mostly closed by a tuned constant rule (declared post-hoc)

Branch `heatpump` (worktree, based on `master` `c3f13a8`, which contains Befund 99). *Numbering:* entered as Befund 101 on merge (2026-10-19). Full text, tables, partner questions: `docs/21_heat_pump.md`. **Scenario band on placeholders, not a plant statement; every number carries its scenario; annual figures are day values x 365.** No RL.

**Question.** Does a heat pump that lifts waste heat (humid exhaust, compressor cooling water) to 60-90 degC and replaces gas or steam heat pay, by CO2 (electricity 0.366 and variant 2030 0.20 kg/kWh, gas 0.201) and by cost (gas 0.030-0.060, electricity 0.12-0.20 EUR/kWh, CO2 price 55/150/300 EUR/t), and does heat pump plus storage under a time-varying power signal need foresight (gate for RL/MPC)? Pre-registration in the docstring of `scripts/gate_heat_pump.py` (commit `37fa2e9`, before any computation on plant data): Stage-B gate L1 = some realistic cell with rule gap `D >= 2` points (programme with perfect foresight against the best of three rules without foresight, in points of the objective without pump and storage); L2 = none, but storage gain `G >= 5 %`; L3 = neither.

**Method (new package `twinlink_ml.heatpump`, tests `tests/test_heatpump*.py`).** Streams and site of storage test 1 (Befund 99), both readings of the exhaust of plant C (volume flow, annual figure). COP = min(quality x Carnot, 8), quality 0.45/0.50/0.55; evaporator and condenser as isothermal pseudo-streams in the same problem table (approach `dT_min/2`, condensation of the exhaust allowed), so the pinch rule (across: dU = Q; above: dU = W; below: 0) follows from the table and is tested; baseline = pinch target with maximum direct recovery. Stage A: exact best output per 15-minute step, best design of the grid (T_e 5-70, T_k 60-90 degC, lift 20-60 K), 528 scenarios x 8 sizes x 3 qualities x 29 criteria, four references with own pinch calculation, break-even and quality sweeps, one-at-a-time sensitivity. Stage B: one storage (40-70 degC, 0.5-5 MWh), signal = mean x (1 + A shape) (A 0-1; bands: price 0-0.6, CO2 0-0.4); HiGHS programme over 24 h / 1 week (and daily state-neutral), rules `myopic`, `gas_value`, `trailing` with an exact step optimum (equals HiGHS in tests); 1600 runs. Checks: programme with C = 0 equals the step dispatch in all runs; storage balance 5.6e-10 kWh. Artifacts `gate_heat_pump` (script `dad1d80`, clean tree, `git/dirty=False`), `gate_heat_pump_tables`, `gate_heat_pump_stage_b_maps` (aggregations), `gate_heat_pump_rule_tuning_posthoc` (declared post-hoc, script `87bc625` committed before its run).

**Result Stage A.** Every scenario of the main grid saves under every central criterion. At 1000 kW, quality 0.50: CO2 today median 265 t/a [7-893] (up to 7.8 % of the site's 11 500 t/a), CO2 2030 356 [52-1334], cost today 37 kEUR/a [0.4-130], cost 300 EUR/t 141 [4-504]. Saving saturates at 250-1000 kW (the hot-utility deficit below 80 degC reachable by the condenser). Own pinch: plant A alone is pinched at shifted 75 degC (top of the compressor heat), the pump works as a booster of compressor heat (55 -> 90, COP 5.2; RA3: 262 t/a, 46 kEUR/a, payback 6.5 a at 600 EUR/kW); with plant C by volume flow the pinch is at about 50 degC (RA1: 35 -> 90, COP 3.3, 497 t/a, 53 kEUR/a, payback 5.6 a at 500 kW); with plant C by annual figure at 13-18 degC (RA2: 201 t/a, 18 kEUR/a, payback 16 a). Break-even COP: CO2 1.55 today, 0.85 in 2030; cost 2.66 / 1.94 / 1.36 at 55 / 150 / 300 EUR/t; the chosen reference designs reach COP 2.9-6.1. All pump heat is delivered in pinch-straddling steps except under the 2030 factor, where even direct electric heating beats gas on CO2. Sensitivity ranking (RA1, CO2 today): exhaust-C reading (-296 t/a), heat-pump approach 20 K (-245), compressor level 400 kW and temperatures 90-50 (-201 each), mode shift (-170), condensing limit 80 degC (-162), `dT_min` 10 K (-151), heater efficiency (+125/-99); cost: gas price (+86 kEUR/a at 0.060), electricity price (+41 at 0.12). Exhaust humidity, solid fraction, `T_kalt`: near 0.

**Result Stage B.** **L1.** 4480 realistic cells; 114 (2.5 %, 62 runs) with `D >= 2` points, 700 (15.6 %) with `G >= 5 %`; largest `D` 9.2 points (A, product 2, week, flat, 1000 kW, CO2 2030, amplitude 0.4, 5 MWh), largest `G` 20.7 %. Site A 104 cells, A+C 10; criteria CO2 2030 42, cost 150 34, cost 300 20, CO2 today 14, cost today 4; modes shift 76, flat 36, weekly 2. Two mechanisms: (a) in the ASSUMED shift mode the compressor source is scarce at night and the programme pre-charges with pump heat in the evening (gaps up to 4.0 points at a constant signal); (b) signal arbitrage, where the named rules mis-value stored heat. **Declared post-hoc:** a constant value of stored heat tuned per cell in hindsight leaves 18 of the 114 cells (all mode shift), largest gap 2.7 points (from 9.2), median 0.8 (from 2.4). Signal swing alone (mode flat): under cost never `D >= 2` points inside the band (max 1.2); under CO2 from an amplitude of 0.1-0.2 with 1-5 MWh. Pre-registered references RB1/RB2 (A+C, product 1, cost today, A 0.4): `D` = 0.

**Caveats.** (1) The letter L1 is the best case over the bands; it says that foresight beats these three rules somewhere, not that RL is needed: a tuned or schedule-aware rule or a day-ahead MPC closes most of it, and the surviving cells rest on the assumed compressor night profile. (2) Two measured days, day x 365; baseline with ideal direct recovery (against today's partial use of compressor heat the pump would look better, partly by direct recovery). (3) COP model optimistic for small-lift boosters (cap 8); isothermal exchangers; the design grid stops at 90 degC (the variant "condensing limit 100 degC" therefore has no effect). (4) One heater efficiency for steam and burner; prices, 2030 factor, capital cost and signal shape are placeholders. (5) 48 Stage-B runs have a non-converged rule (none of them in an L1 cell); in 2 the rule lies 0.07 points below the programme. (6) The factor-4.9 contradiction of plant C (Befund 99) is the largest Stage-A sensitivity. Questions for the partner in `docs/21`, section 8 (exhaust-C reading, exchanger approaches, compressor heat time series and temperatures, supply-air and condensing temperature first).

*Addendum to Befund 101 (2026-10-16): solid fraction from study 4 (Befund 103).* The parallel study 4 (branch `plant-a-operating-point`, `docs/23` section 5) shows from the energy balance of the two measured days of plant A that the solid fraction must be larger (product-specific minima kept locally); its reference 0.634 (band 0.60-0.70, placeholder) replaces the Befund-99 value 0.3, which is inadmissible (at 0.3 the product-2 exhaust was capped at saturation in every step). The results above are kept as the variant "Befund-99 assumption"; the unchanged pre-registered grids were rerun with 0.634 (option `--solid-fraction`, script `3603fb3`, clean tree; artifacts `gate_heat_pump_sf0634`, `gate_heat_pump_tables_sf0634`, `gate_heat_pump_stage_b_maps_sf0634`, `gate_heat_pump_rule_tuning_posthoc_sf0634`, comparison `gate_heat_pump_solid_fraction_comparison`; `docs/21` section 9). Study 4 against Befund 99: exhaust heat of plant A 604 / 825 kW (product 1), product 2 no longer capped. Stage A: still every scenario saves; median at 1000 kW CO2 today 244 / 265 t/a, CO2 2030 328 / 356, cost today 34.3 / 37.1 kEUR/a, cost 300 130 / 141 (about -8 %); RA1 483 / 497 t/a, RA2 (plant C by annual figure) 154 / 201 t/a, RA3/RA4 (plant A alone, pinched by compressor heat) unchanged. Stage B: **L1 / L1**, 121 / 114 cells with `D >= 2` points, 821 / 700 with `G >= 5 %`, largest `D` 9.2 / 9.2 points; after the declared post-hoc tuned constant 18 / 18 cells remain, all in mode shift. Readings and conclusions unchanged.
### Befund 102 (2026-10-16): exhaust recirculation of one line -- at re-optimised set points the moisture limit is paid for with inlet temperature, the CO2 of the lab line falls by 17 % in the median (envelope), and recirculation makes the line's own heat recovery possible instead of competing with it; at unchanged set points there is no headroom

Branch `exhaust-recirc`, merged into `master` on 2026-10-19 (entered as Befund 102). Full text, tables, partner questions: `docs/22_exhaust_recirc.md`. **Laboratory line with placeholder physics; recovery figures lab x k (D4); the transfer grid is a set of placeholders, not a plant statement.** No RL.

**Model.** Optional `OperationConfig.exhaust_recirculation_fraction` `r` and `EnergyConfig.recirculation_duct_loss_coefficient` (commit `e1eccbc`): the inlet air is the mixture of fresh air and bed exhaust ahead of the heater, the heater books from the mixing temperature, a cube-law recirculation fan is added. Unset: not in the fingerprint (all nine config fingerprints unchanged) and the fresh-air path bit-identical to `c3f13a8` (float-hex test). The humidity fixed point of the loop is solved by a bracketed root search on a monotone residual; a damped Picard iteration as in the fresh-air path does not converge there (relative errors above 1 at r = 0.8). Mixing water and enthalpy balances and the loop water balance close to 1e-12 (tests); the steady-state solver needs no change; at r = 0.95 and a cold point no steady state exists (drying capacity collapses).

**Design (fixed in `scripts/run_exhaust_recirc.py`, commit `44a331c`, before any run).** 25 Befund-52 contexts; objective CO2 with the gas-fired heater booking of M1 incl. fan power; quality limit 0.15 with margin m; u >= 1.26 m/s; arms G (r fixed on 0..0.8, plus 0.9), R (r free in [0, 0.95]), J0/J (CO2 after the recovery cascade of M2 as objective); sensitivity on the 3 x 3 sub-grid. DE budget reduced to maxiter 20; anchor gate (< 0.5 % CO2 against M1 and against maxiter 50): **passed** (largest difference 6.5e-4; `r*` itself only to about +-0.03). Artifacts `exhaust_recirc_anchor`, `_main`, `_sensitivity`, `_analysis` (`06d6356`, `d665851`, `eaf105e`, `d40613d`), all `git/dirty=False`.

**Results (lab).** (i) At unchanged set points (the r = 0 optimum) the admissible r is 0.002 at the 17 of 25 contexts where the moisture limit already binds, 0.035-0.18 at the other 8. (ii) With re-optimised set points every grid r up to 0.8 is feasible at all 25 contexts; CO2 saving against r = 0 at r = 0.8: 15.0 % median (-13.7..28.7 %), inlet temperature 60.3 -> 81.0 degC, exhaust dew point 23.6 -> 46.0 degC (medians). (iii) Best r per context (envelope over R and G, **declared post hoc**: R was beaten by the grid at 9 of 25 warm contexts, bimodal landscape): median 0.86 (p10 0.10), CO2 saving 17.0 % median (p10 0.4 %, max 29.1 %), heater gas 19.3 %; 29-25 % at 5 degC, 14-20 % at 20 degC, 0-15 % at 27.5-35 degC (Spearman with the ambient temperature -0.89). Binding at the best point: moisture 24/25, u within 0.01 m/s of 1.26 at 17/25; bed temperature, inlet box and fog do not bind. (iv) Recovery (lab x k): at the r = 0 optimum the exhaust (32-44 degC) is too cold for `dT_min` 20 K (0 kW at 17/25); with recirculation 12.6 kW median are recovered and the CO2 saving of recirculation rises to 20.4 % (J against J0). Only an exchanger BEFORE the mixing point (fresh-air side) recovers; after it (mixed air) nothing at any grid point. (v) Sensitivity of the median saving: saturation degree 0.45 +6.6, critical moisture 0.25 +6.1 / 0.17 -4.2, quality limit 0.20 -2.0 (fog binds at 5/9), u >= 0.80 m/s -1.3, GAB parameters <= 0.6 points.

**Transfer (placeholders).** Lab median heater-gas fraction 19.3 % applied to the partner's orders of magnitude: plant A about 1570 MWh/a, 315 t CO2/a (2.7 % of the site); plant C 1810 MWh/a (volume reading) or 369 MWh/a (annual reading, factor 4.9 of Befund 99). Mixing alone at the measured plant-A exhaust temperatures (34.4 / 60.7 degC) gives 14 / 28 % of the heater duty at r = 0.4; the exhaust humidity headroom ranges from 0 (cool, wet exhaust) to 0.96.

**Caveats.** Placeholder kinetics (the top of the sensitivity ranking); inlet humidity up to 0.18 kg/kg at the best points, outside the range the kinetics were set for; no modelled limit for duct condensation, stickiness, hygiene, dust; steady state only; direct firing (plant C) adds combustion water, not modelled. Questions for the partner: `docs/22`, section 8 (exhaust state and water load per product first).
### Befund 103 (2026-10-16): operating point of plant A -- another air flow and supply temperature saves at most 758 kg CO2/d (14.6 %) on product 1 and 90 kg CO2/d (2.8 %) on product 2 at the reference placeholders; the result is decided by the minimum air flow, the fan law and the waste-heat side

Branch `plant-a-operating-point` (merged into `master` on 2026-10-19). *Numbering:* entered as Befund 103 on merge. Details, tables, placeholders and partner questions: `docs/23_plant_a_operating_point.md`. Code `src/twinlink_ml/plant_a_op/`, tests `tests/test_plant_a_op.py`. Pre-registration: docstring of `scripts/study_plant_a_operating_point.py` (commit `2b41d9d`, committed before any optimisation; before it only the day means, the closure of the dryer balance over the solid fraction and the two-point fan exponents had been looked at). Artifact `artifacts/runs/study_plant_a_operating_point.json` (run on `2b41d9d`, clean tree, `git/dirty=False`, committed as `7bc187a`). **Every number is an upper bound under placeholders and proxy constraints; the proxies do not replace a product-moisture measurement; no operating recommendation.**

**Question.** What would another combination of process-air flow and supply-air temperature at plant A save in CO2 against today's operation, counting steam (gas boiler) and the electricity of both fans?

**Method.** Stationary balance at plant scale on the day means of the two measured days (within a day the air flow moves by less than 0.3 %), production held: dryer energy balance (evaporation = spray rate x (1 - solid fraction), wall loss `UA` fitted on one day), steam via the air balance as in Befund 91 (preheater duty measured, conductance fitted per day; at another air flow either the water inlet is held, `fixed_water_inlet`, or the duty, `duty_held`), fans `P ~ V^n` anchored per day (`data_fit` n = 0.51 from the process fan between the days; `affinity` n = 3 placeholder), CO2 0.201 kg/kWh gas / 0.366 (or 0.20, 2030 placeholder) kg/kWh electricity. Constraints: (a) outlet temperature >= observed minimum per product, (b) reconstructed relative exhaust humidity <= observed maximum, (a and b); minimum air fraction 0.6-0.9 (fluidisation placeholder). Search air factor 0.6-1.1 x supply 70-100 degC on a grid with refinement; the measured point is always a candidate. Main grid 18 432 searches (2 products x 4 weathers x 4 solid fractions x 2 calibration days x 2 waste-heat variants x 2 fan laws x 3 boiler efficiencies x 2 electricity factors x 3 constraints x 4 minimum air fractions; 2 304 of them inadmissible because the calibration day gives `UA` < 0 at solid fraction 0.60), plus one-at-a-time sensitivity.

**Result.** Today (model baseline, reference placeholders): 5 206 / 3 196 kg CO2/d (product 1 / 2), of which fans 39.5 % / 46.9 %. Reference optimum (measured weather, solid fraction 0.65, own-day `UA`, `fixed_water_inlet`, `data_fit`, eta 0.88, 0.366, constraint (a), minimum air 0.8): **758 kg/d (14.6 %)** on product 1 at air factor 0.80 / 90.4 degC (steam 535, fans 223 kg/d) and **90 kg/d (2.8 %)** on product 2 at 0.80 / 94.7 degC (steam -69, fans +160: less air takes 55 kW less waste heat from the preheater at the measured water inlet). The proxy binds in almost every cell, together with the minimum air fraction or the 100 degC limit. Range at the measured weather over all placeholders: 73-2 649 kg/d (product 1), 0-2 109 kg/d (product 2). Annualised (x 365, 24/7): 277 / 33 t/a, 155 t/a for a 50/50 mix (placeholder), about 1.3 % of the site's 11 500 t/a.

**Sensitivity ranking** (one at a time, largest change of the saving, kg/d): minimum air fraction 690 > fan law 561 > waste-heat variant 306 > constraint variant 125 > calibration day 103 > electricity factor 101 > weather 80 > boiler efficiency 23 > solid fraction 11 > fan heat fraction, room temperature, intake humidity, feed and atomising-air temperature, cp of the solids (each <= 7).

**Calibration check.** The balance needs a larger solid fraction than the 0.3 of Befund 99 (wall loss >= 0; product-specific minima kept locally); one shared solid fraction and `UA` fit both days only at 0.634 / 0.93 kW/K; at the reference 0.65 the transfer misses the pre-registered 2 K (outlet error +1.4 K one way, -3.5 K the other), at 0.70-0.75 by 5-16 K. The fan data cannot identify any exponent (within-day flow CV 0.05-0.10 %; the exhaust fan's two-point exponent 8.8 is unphysical and not used).

**Report, not fixed (for the managing session).** The solid fraction 0.3 (band 0.2-0.5) used for the reconstructed exhaust humidity of plant A in Befund 99 is inadmissible by the energy balance of the same days; it enters Befund 99 only through that humidity. Not changed here; taken up on 2026-10-19 by the addendum to Befund 99 (re-check with an admissible solid fraction).

**Partner questions** (by influence): minimum air flow per product; fan control (speed or damper) and fan curves; whether the storage loop delivers its heat at a lower air flow (water temperature limits); the operator's moisture criterion and the admissible supply temperature; solid fraction / suspension density per product; steam or gas metering and boiler efficiency; one exhaust-humidity measurement.

**Tests.** Full suite at commit `2b41d9d` (code identical to the branch head; later commits add only the artifact and documentation): 1074 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed (counted from the progress dots; the `-q` configuration prints no summary line), exit code 0; new tests `tests/test_plant_a_op.py` (19, synthetic data, including a check that no measurement-point or equipment codes appear in the new files). `test_denylist.py` ran with `local/denylist.txt` and passed after the documentation commit; ruff clean; mypy clean on `src/twinlink_ml/plant_a_op` and the study script.

Against the static regression in the same cells (single descriptive paired tests, uncorrected, not in any family): the xLSTM median is 3.4 (excited) and 2.3 (constant holdout) times the static one at `n_train` 64, the xLSTM worse in 4 and 3 of 5 seeds, **not resolved** at 64 (p 0.11, 0.18); resolved worse only at `n_train` 8 and 16 (excited) and 8 (constant holdout); ratios 2.3-4.3 over all budgets.

### Addendum (2026-10-19) to Befund 94: how often the training in arm N reaches the epoch cap (fixed training budget)

Addendum to Befund 94 (no existing finding changed). Pure re-analysis of the committed records `rerun_full_N.jsonl`, no training, no new data. Script `scripts/analyze_94_epoch_cap.py` (commit `a36bcea`, committed before the run; rule in its docstring; test `tests/test_analyze_94_epoch_cap.py`; a later commit `0fda89a` only ends the first docstring line with a period), artifact `befund94_addendum_epoch_cap_rerun_full` (commit `6930205`, clean tree, `git/dirty=False`). Reason: review 4b (N4) reports, from its own computation, that the epoch cap shapes the comparison more widely than the sentence on the Transformer in `docs/08` says. **Unit:** one training of one head (target) of one network; the records repeat the same training for every evaluation variant and test set, so they are de-duplicated by (network, seed, `n_train`): 5 networks x 4 budgets x 5 seeds = 100 trainings, 3 heads each = 60 head-trainings per network over all budgets, 15 per budget. **Cap:** the recorded `net_max_epochs` = 200, one fixed protocol for all networks (early stopping with patience 20, no tuning); a head "reaches the cap" if it ran all 200 epochs.

**Result (head-trainings that reach the cap, of 15 per budget and of 60 over all budgets; the same table by head is in the artifact).**

| network | n_train 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | all budgets | by head over all budgets (energy / moisture / bed temperature, each of 20) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GRU | 11 | 10 | 8 | 4 | 33 of 60 | 17 / 3 / 13 |
| LSTM | 10 | 10 | 7 | 5 | 32 of 60 | 18 / 1 / 13 |
| Transformer | 10 | 12 | 12 | 10 | 44 of 60 | 19 / 5 / 20 |
| xLSTM | 0 | 0 | 2 | 2 | 4 of 60 | 1 / 3 / 0 |
| Mamba | 3 | 7 | 3 | 9 | 22 of 60 | 13 / 1 / 8 |

At `n_train` 64 (the budget of the main statements): Transformer 10 of 15 (energy 4, moisture 1, bed temperature 5), Mamba 9 of 15 (4 / 0 / 5), LSTM 5 of 15 (3 / 0 / 2), GRU 4 of 15 (3 / 0 / 1), xLSTM 2 of 15 (0 / 2 / 0). All cap hits have their best epoch within the last 20 epochs, except one GRU head (32 of 33; LSTM 32 of 32, Transformer 44 of 44, xLSTM 4 of 4, Mamba 22 of 22): the curve was still improving, or at least still setting its minimum, when the budget ended. **Reading:** the fixed budget of 200 epochs binds for a large part of the heads of the GRU, LSTM, Transformer and Mamba, mostly on the energy and bed-temperature heads and, for the GRU and LSTM, mostly at the small budgets (more steps per epoch at larger `n_train`); the moisture head rarely reaches it. The Transformer is not the only network affected (review 4b counted 20 of 30 for the Transformer at `n_train` 64 against 10 of 15 here, 18 of 30 for Mamba against 9 of 15, LSTM 10 of 30 against 5 of 15, GRU 8 of 30 against 4 of 15, xLSTM 4 of 30 against 2 of 15: the same shares, double denominators because the reviewer counted the records of both test sets; the de-duplicated counts above are the ones to quote).

**Caveats.** Counts only: nothing says how much lower the error would be with a larger cap, only that the comparison is made at a fixed training budget that binds for part of the heads, so rank statements hold for this budget and this protocol (as `docs/08` already says for the untuned configuration). Arm-N records only; the old data A0 are not re-counted here.

### Befund 104 (2026-10-19): convergence check of Befund 94 at 600 epochs -- no head reaches the new cap, the order GRU >= LSTM > Transformer on energy and bed temperature stands, two Holm verdicts of the Transformer drop out; pre-registered reading: none of K1-K3 (decision to the project lead); addendum to Befund 94

Addendum to Befund 94 and to its addendum on the epoch cap (no number of either entry is changed). Branch `convergence-check`. Question: does a larger training budget change the order or the gaps on energy and bed temperature? Driver `scripts/run_convergence_check_94.py` and analysis `scripts/analyze_convergence_check_94.py` (commit `e4923ec`, committed before the run; cells, families, gate, readings and cost estimate fixed in their docstrings; tests `tests/test_convergence_check_94.py`). Records `conv600_main_N.jsonl.gz` (240, compressed; commit `ec0fb6a`, run at `e4923ec`, clean tree, `git/dirty=False`) and `conv600_main_timing.json`; artifact `convergence_check_94_conv600_main_attempt2` (commit `294c9ea`, run at `46b8a8c`, clean tree, `git/dirty=False`, `code/package_dir` `src/twinlink_ml`).

**What was run.** Arm N of Befund 94 (`DataSpec.new_study()`, preset version 2), same data, seeds 1-5, splits, holdout (seed 999) and configuration, `run_arch_rerun_worker.py` unchanged; **only change `max_epochs` 600 instead of 200**, patience 20 unchanged. GRU, LSTM, Transformer at `n_train` 16 and 64 (30 jobs, 8 workers). Metric `rmse_run_median_physical`, primary variant of arm N, h = 1 and 36, both test sets (excited, constant-run holdout); paired t over five seeds per cell. Primary cells: energy and bed temperature (16 per pair); moisture only at `n_train` 64, as a control.

**Gate: passed in attempt 2, with one disclosed correction.** Attempt 1 (kept, `convergence_check_94_conv600_main.json`, commit `d724fda`) failed formally on 24 checks, all on the wall-clock metric `inference_us_per_window` (a time measurement, not a function of the weights); every history and every error metric agreed. The metric comparison now excludes that one metric (commit `46b8a8c`); no tolerance, cell, family or reading was changed. Result: fingerprints and model parameters equal Befund 94 for all 240 records; the validation-loss histories of the first min(E200, E600) epochs equal Befund 94 for all 90 head-trainings (relative tolerance 1e-6); every head that stopped before 200 in Befund 94 stops at the same epoch. The 600-epoch run is an exact continuation of Befund 94.

**Epochs.** None of the 90 head-trainings reaches 600; all 51 that reached 200 in Befund 94 (47 of the 60 on energy and bed temperature) now stop by early stopping. Largest epoch counts: GRU 479, LSTM 519, Transformer 587 (all `n_train` 16, energy). Medians of the epochs on energy and bed temperature at 600: GRU 303.5 / 178 (`n_train` 16 / 64), LSTM 255.5 / 193.5, Transformer 334 / 302.

**Verdicts against the reference over the 16 primary cells (uncorrected, B = candidate better / W = worse / u = unresolved; median over the cells of the ratio of the medians, candidate / reference).**

| pair | 200 epochs | 600 epochs | ratio 200 -> 600 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GRU against LSTM | 5B / 0W / 11u | 3B / 0W / 13u | 0.979 -> 0.973 |
| Transformer against LSTM | 0B / 13W / 3u | 0B / 11W / 5u | 1.212 -> 1.208 |
| Transformer against GRU | 0B / 13W / 3u | 0B / 15W / 1u | 1.231 -> 1.204 |

Changed uncorrected verdicts: GRU against LSTM, better -> unresolved at `n_train` 16 excited energy h36 and at 64 constant-run holdout bed temperature h36. Transformer against LSTM, worse -> unresolved at 16 excited energy h36, 16 constant-run holdout energy h1, 64 excited bed temperature h1; unresolved -> worse at 64 constant-run holdout bed temperature h36. Transformer against GRU, unresolved -> worse at 64 constant-run holdout energy h36 and bed temperature h36. No cell is against the order at 600 (no GRU worse than LSTM, no Transformer better than LSTM or GRU).

**Holm (main family: the 336 rank cells of arm N, 40 cells substituted by their 600-epoch values).** Befund 94 counts reproduced (260 uncorrected / 70 after Holm); with the substitution 256 / 67. Two Holm verdicts of the primary cells change, both Transformer against LSTM at `n_train` 16, excited test set: energy h1 and bed temperature h36, worse after Holm -> not resolved after Holm; both stay resolved uncorrected with all five seeds worse (ratio of the medians 1.72 -> 1.43 and 1.65 -> 1.55; p 4e-6 -> 0.009 and 2e-5 -> 5e-4). No GRU-against-LSTM cell is resolved after Holm at 200 or 600. Sensitivity families: the 40 cells alone, Transformer worse after Holm 5 -> 2; the 20 Transformer-against-GRU cells alone 7 -> 2.

**Control (moisture, `n_train` 64).** Verdicts and ratios unchanged at 600 for all three pairs (the moisture heads reached 200 in at most one seed per network).

**Same network, 600 against 200 epochs (change of the median over seeds; excited, h1 / h36).** Energy at `n_train` 16: Transformer -22.4 % / -17.3 %, LSTM -6.8 % / -15.7 %, GRU -5.1 % / -10.2 %; at 64: LSTM -8.8 % / -12.5 %, Transformer -5.6 % / -8.6 %, GRU -0.2 % / -2.2 %. Bed temperature, h36: Transformer -9.1 % (16) and -8.6 % (64), GRU -6.5 % / 0.0 %, LSTM -3.2 % / 0.0 %. On the constant-run holdout the changes are of the same sign or near zero (largest: Transformer energy at 16, -13.8 % / -14.6 %; largest increase LSTM bed temperature h36 at 16, +4.9 %). The Transformer gains most at `n_train` 16, but not enough to close the gap.

**Pre-registered reading: none.** Not K3 (no cell against the order); not K2 (Transformer worse than LSTM 13 -> 11 cells, against GRU 13 -> 15, neither halved); not K1, because two Holm verdicts of the main family change. By the rule fixed beforehand, the consequence is left to the project lead. What the numbers show: the order and the uncorrected gaps on energy and bed temperature survive the larger budget (median ratio Transformer / LSTM 1.21 at both budgets), the GRU advantage over the LSTM gets smaller (5 -> 3 uncorrected cells, none after Holm at either budget), and the Holm-resolved part of the Transformer deficit in the main family is thin at `n_train` 16 (two cells sit near the Holm threshold).

**Run time.** 452.5 min wall time, 8 workers, 50.0 core-hours of job wall time; longest job Transformer `n_train` 64 seed 2, 7.5 h. The estimate made beforehand (134 core-hours and 25 h worst case) was too high for two reasons: no head ran to 600, and the Transformer at `n_train` 64 needed 29.8 s per epoch and head against 54.1 s in the records of Befund 94 (median over seeds of `training/elapsed_s` / epochs run, from the artifact rows; GRU and LSTM equal within 5 %); the cause of the difference was not examined.

**Caveats.** Budget 600 with patience 20 only; xLSTM, Mamba and the baselines not retrained (their cells keep the 200-epoch reference); `n_train` 8 and 32 not run; arm N only. Five seeds, four degrees of freedom; cells of a channel are not independent. *Numbering:* prepared as Befund 104 on the branch; entered as Befund 104 on merge (2026-10-20).

**Decision of the project lead (2026-10-20; added after the fact, the entry above is unchanged).** (1) **Gate correction confirmed:** the wall-clock metric `inference_us_per_window` is not reproducible (it is a time measurement, not a function of the weights) and does not belong in the comparison, as in Befund 94; attempt 1 stays in the record as the disclosed first attempt, attempt 2 is the gate of the check. (2) **Reading:** none of the pre-registered readings K1-K3 applies exactly; the decision is **"K1 in substance with two borderline Holm changes"**: every head stops before 600 epochs, the order and the effect sizes are stable, and two Transformer-against-LSTM cells at `n_train` 16 (excited test set: energy h1, bed temperature h36) drop narrowly out of the Holm resolution; they stay resolved uncorrected, with all five seeds worse. Befund 94 remains the main result; Befund 104 is its robustness check against the training budget.

### Befund [number assigned on merge] (2026-10-22): dynamic headroom in continuous operation -- MPC without disturbance preview saves 0.55 % energy over quasi-stationary RTO in the median (perfect preview 1.51 %), almost entirely through a smaller margin; pre-registered reading L0, candidate "robust control" not open

Branch `dynamic-headroom`, study document `docs/24_dynamic_headroom.md`. Question: is there an energy gain from dynamic operation over quasi-stationary RTO when disturbances are ridden out in continuous operation? (Headroom test before any further RL work; all earlier RL tests were memoryless problems.) Driver `scripts/run_dynamic_headroom.py`, analysis `scripts/analyze_dynamic_headroom.py` with the reading fixed in its docstring (commit `d30a83f`, before the first run); main run `dynamic_headroom_v2` (commit `5a38798`, clean tree), analysis `dynamic_headroom_v2_analysis.json`. **Placeholders (every number inherits them):** quality limit 0.15 kg/kg as a path condition at every 5 s sample, u_min 0.80 m/s, start margin 0.01, all scenario amplitudes (those of the family "observed" derived from plant data, relative only), second product 0.12 / 0.25, GAB band of the robustness variant, gas-heater efficiency 0.80, soft-constraint weight, the whole lab-line process config.

**Set-up.** Truth = the unchanged grey-box model (GAB placeholder config of the bandit line, 4 states, RK4, 5 s); no surrogate. Controllers command inlet temperature and gas velocity every 5 min: R0 fixed point, R1 quasi-stationary RTO (steady optimum at the current disturbance), R2 preview optimum (multiple shooting over 24 h, true disturbance course), R3 MPC without disturbance preview (2 h, receding); CasADi/IPOPT on the same model equations (symbolic backend of the existing physics functions, test against the truth RHS to 1e-10). Each controller gets the smallest family-wide moisture margin with which the path condition holds in every scenario (bisection, tolerance 2.5e-4 kg/kg). Solid fraction: the lab line's own band around 0.30 (decision of the project lead); at a plant-like 0.60-0.70 the 0.15 limit does not bind on this line (steady moisture 0.07-0.11 kg/kg at the inlet-temperature minimum) -- whether it binds on the plant is an open question to the application partner, not a result of this study.

**Margins (kg/kg).** Observed (105 scenarios of 24 h): R0 0.04355, R1 0.00664, R3 0.00270, R2 0.00021. Stress (80): R0 0.07129, R1 0.01680, R3 0.01224, R2 0.00013.

**Gaps, observed (median, range).** R1 -> R3: **0.55 %** (0.05 .. 1.50 %); R1 -> R2 (upper bound): 1.51 % (1.02 .. 2.44 %); R0 -> R1: 8.93 % (0.69 .. 25.23 %). Decomposition of R1 -> R3: margin share 0.92 %, trajectory share -0.35 %; in the type with an inlet-temperature fluctuation below the command grid (sigma 1.5 K, 4 min): margin 0.93 %, trajectory -0.75 %, gap 0.19 %. The preview optimum's gap is margin as well (1.49 of 1.51 %). Stress (upper estimate, no reading): R1 -> R3 0.71 % (-0.69 .. 1.71 %), R1 -> R2 3.89 % (3.28 .. 6.29 %).

**Pre-registered reading: L0** (pooled median < 2 %; no type in another class): dynamic control does not pay in continuous operation of this line; by the rule fixed beforehand, the RL line for the granulator is to be closed. **Robustness:** with 20 isotherm draws R1 holds at its nominal margin in 19 of 20 draws, R3 in 20 of 20; cost against the nominal margins R1 -0.23 %, R3 0.00 % -> candidate "robust control" not open. Caveat (design, found in the evaluation): R1's per-draw search started at 0 on the 10-scenario subset, R3's at its nominal margin; the negative R1 cost only says the subset needs less than the family-wide margin. The cost relative to the subset's own nominal margin was not computed.

**Product change (per changeover, margins of "observed").** Tightening the moisture target 0.15 -> 0.12: R1 needs 37-55 min to reach the new specification, R3 0.9-1.8 min at +0.35 % energy, R2 dries ahead and exceeds the new limit by 0.0010-0.0027 kg/kg for 20-25 s after the change (soft-constraint weight). Energy per changeover against R1: R2 -1.2 % to -2.6 %, R3 -1.9 % to +0.35 % (medians per direction). R2 used the R1 schedule in 2 of 20 changeovers (safeguard). Frequency of changeovers unknown, not extrapolated.

**Numerics.** The rate-limit ramp had to be modelled in the optimiser (mean of the ramp per RK4 step); without it the preview optimum's moisture prediction was off by up to 9e-3 kg/kg. A default IPOPT start found a chattering local optimum worse than the R1 schedule on an undisturbed scenario; R2 starts at the R1 schedule and never takes a plan its own model rates worse. No solver failure in the main run.

**Run time.** 29.4 h on 14 workers (R3 searches 6.5 h observed, 10.1 h stress, 6.7 h robustness), plus 5.5 h of the aborted attempt 1 (`dynamic_headroom_v1`, commit `d30a83f`: memory exhausted by one SX MPC solver per scenario; restarted from scratch with the R3 optimiser as MX, `5a38798`; no artifact of attempt 1).

**Caveats.** One lab line, 4-state model; controllers see the true state (no estimator, no noise); family-wide margins; the optional time-varying CO2 signal was not run; transfer to the plant depends on whether the moisture limit binds there.
